Author: Star Business Desk

Title: ShopUp partners with Sarona, ADI Australia on leadership programme
Content:
B2B commerce platform ShopUp, in collaboration with Sarona and ADI Australia, facilitated Project Arohi, a leadership development programme focused on strengthening the capabilities of ShopUp employees.

Through the eight-session programme, employees enhanced their communication, stakeholder management, data-driven decision-making, adaptive leadership and workplace resilience, while developing a stronger understanding of gender equality, diversity and social inclusion (GEDSI).

Queentries Regar, technical assistance manager at Sarona Asset Management, conducted the session along with other mentors.

Delivered in partnership with the Bangladesh Youth Leadership Centre (BYLC), the programme reflects ShopUp’s continued commitment to building leadership capabilities and investing in the development of its people.

Commenting on the programme, Ataur Rahim Chowdhury, chief executive officer of ShopUp Bangladesh, said, “Developing strong leaders is a long-term investment in ShopUp’s future. Project Arohi has provided our employees with the skills and perspectives to lead more effectively and contribute to building the market leaders of tomorrow.”
Author: Star Business Desk

Title: Crowne Plaza brings seafood party to Dhaka
Content:
Crowne Plaza Dhaka Gulshan is hosting a seafood-themed dining event from September 10 to 19, featuring a range of seafood dishes, live grilling and tableside service.

The Seafood Party is offering dishes, including Shrimp cocktail, Oysters, Mussels, Tuna and Octopus salad, seafood bisque, salt-crusted Salmon, seafood Paella, Prawn teriyaki, fried Calamari and freshly prepared sushi, according to a press release.

Guests can also select fresh fish and seafood for grilling at a live fish grill operated by the hotel’s culinary team.

Another feature of the event is a crab and lobster platter served at the table by Executive Chef Kassem.

The event is priced at Tk 7,999 net per person. Selected cardholders of Mutual Trust Bank (MTB), the prime partner of the event, will be eligible for a Buy 1 Get 3 offer, allowing four people to dine for the price of one.

The offer brings the effective cost to Tk 1,999.75 net per person when four guests dine together using an eligible MTB card.

Selected bank cardholders will also be able to avail themselves of Buy 1 Get 1 and Buy 1 Get 2 offers, the release said.

Karthi VK, general manager of Crowne Plaza Dhaka Gulshan, said the hotel wanted to create a seafood experience that went beyond a regular dinner.

“We wanted to create a seafood experience that feels less like a regular dinner and more like a celebration. From the live grill and fresh seafood to the chef-served crab and lobster, there will be plenty to explore, share and enjoy,” he said.

“Most importantly, we want our guests to come with their favourite people, come hungry and simply have a great time. This is a party for seafood lovers, and we can’t wait to welcome everyone to the table,” he added.
Author: Star Business Desk

Title: Pathao launches platform to simplify business for merchants
Content:
Pathao, the largest digital commerce platform in Bangladesh, has launched Pathao Commerce, an all-in-one platform that brings storefronts, sales channels, orders, inventory, payments, delivery and customer communication together in one place.

Built around three core needs of today’s merchants -- management, efficiency and growth, the platform aims to reduce manual work, simplify everyday operations and help businesses scale more efficiently.

Commenting on the initiative, Fahim Ahmed, chief executive officer of Pathao, said, “For years, merchants have trusted Pathao to take the hassle out of deliveries and help them get their products to customers reliably.

“With Pathao Commerce, we are taking that commitment beyond delivery, giving entrepreneurs a single platform to manage everything from their storefront and orders to inventory, sales, payments, delivery and customer communication.”

The platform enables merchants to manage their product catalogues, orders, payments, inventory and deliveries, while also allowing them to create professional online storefronts.

It also connects with third-party sales channels such as Shopify, WooCommerce and Daraz, allowing merchants to bring their existing sales operations into Pathao Commerce. Sales, orders, inventory and earnings are automatically updated, giving merchants greater visibility and control over their businesses.

For many online merchants, completing a sale involves switching between Facebook Messenger, Instagram DM, WhatsApp, spreadsheets and delivery platforms, often requiring the same information to be entered multiple times.

Pathao Commerce addresses this through a unified chat inbox that brings customer conversations from these channels into one place through official Meta integrations.

Merchants can view order histories within conversations and use AI-enabled support, backed by Pathao’s database of nearly 10 million unique nationwide addresses, to enter delivery information faster.

They can also generate an Instant Checkout link directly within a customer chat window, allowing customers to complete their orders and payments in a single step.

Once an order is placed, a pickup agent is automatically dispatched to the merchant’s doorstep, while a tracking link is immediately shared with the customer.

By reducing platform switching, copy-pasting and manual coordination, Pathao Commerce aims to make the journey from customer conversation to delivery faster and simpler.
Author: Star Business Desk

Title: Week-long exhibition honours Sheikh Rabiul Haque’s artistic legacy
Content:
A week-long art exhibition celebrating the 80-year creative journey of Sheikh Rabiul Haque, a writer, painter, singer and entrepreneur, was inaugurated at the National Art Gallery of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy in Dhaka.

The exhibition will continue until September 18, 2026.

Renowned painter Rafiqun Nabi inaugurated the exhibition as the chief guest, according to a press release.

A cultural programme and discussion session will also be held on September 15 at the National Art Gallery Auditorium of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy.

The event will highlight various aspects of Sheikh Rabiul Haque’s multifaceted creative contributions and his significant journey in the fields of art and culture.

Painter Jyotsna Mahbuba and Kamrul Islam, general secretary of the Bangiya Sahitya Sanskriti Sangsad, along with other notable personalities, were present at the event.
Author: Star Business Desk

Title: Selim Barkat made chairman of FinExcel
Content:
Financial Excellence Ltd (FinExcel) has appointed Selim Barkat as chairman of the company.

Selim brings nearly four decades of leadership experience in banking and financial services in Bangladesh and the United States. His areas of expertise include strategic leadership, corporate governance, risk management, transaction banking, treasury and capital markets, according to a press release.

Most recently, he served as regional general manager of Habib Bank Limited (HBL) for Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and the Maldives. In the role, he helped drive the bank’s strategic transformation in the South Asia region.

Earlier, he held senior positions at Citibank and Citigroup in Bangladesh and New York.

He was involved in global business management and later worked as a portfolio banker covering credit and counterparty-risk portfolios for investment banks, broker-dealers, financial market intermediaries and the North American insurance industry.

He also played a key role in establishing Citibank, National Association’s first branch in Bangladesh.

As chairman, Barkat will bring his international banking experience, strategic vision and focus on risk management and corporate governance to FinExcel.

He holds an MBA in finance from the Institute of Business Administration (IBA) at the University of Dhaka.

He also served as an adjunct faculty member at Rutgers Business School, Rutgers University, US.
Author: Star Business Desk

Title: 13 officials face BB action for deposit incentive irregularity
Content:
Bangladesh Bank has ordered Bangladesh Commerce Bank to take the highest administrative action against 13 officials for allegedly receiving Tk 4 crore from the bank’s funds in the name of incentives under a deposit mobilisation campaign.

Through a letter to the managing director of the bank on August 25, the banking regulator also directed the lender to take legal action over the irregular withdrawal of the money and recover the funds.

The central bank took the decision after a special inspection of Bangladesh Commerce Bank’s head office and principal branch following allegations of misappropriation of Tk 5 crore belonging to depositors.

Contacted, Arief Hossain Khan, executive director and spokesperson of Bangladesh Bank, told The Daily Star that there is no scope for providing any incentive for collecting deposits.

“What happened at the bank was that it collected deposits at a lower rate but showed a higher rate and took the difference as a cash incentive,” said the spokesperson, adding that this is against the policy.

According to the inspection report, Tk 4 crore was deposited into the personal accounts of 13 officials on June 4, 2026, as “incentives” for collecting deposits under the bank’s “Ujjibon” deposit campaign.

The payment was not approved by the bank’s board of directors, the report said.

The 13 officials included eight from the head office, four from the principal branch and one from the bank’s Dilkusha branch.

The money was subsequently withdrawn in cash through 14 cheques over two days.

Nine cheques were used to withdraw Tk 3.04 crore on June 4 this year, while five cheques were used to withdraw Tk 96 lakh on June 7, according to the inspection findings.

The cash was withdrawn by Md Delwar Hossain, senior executive vice president and head of the treasury department of Bangladesh Commerce Bank, and Md Hamidur Rahman, senior principal officer and personal secretary to the managing director.

The two officials reportedly left the principal branch with the cash in the bank’s vehicle after each withdrawal.

Bangladesh Bank has instructed the bank to dismiss Delwar Hossain and Hamidur Rahman. The directive is separate from any previous orders issued against them.

The central bank has also ordered the bank to take the highest administrative action against the other 11 officials involved and inform it of the measures taken within a month.

The other officials are First Assistant Vice President (FAVP) Yusuf Siddiq Ullah, AVP Saleh Ahmed, Officer Sarwar, FAVP Sujon Das, AVP Tasnuba Majumder, AVP Ahsan Habib, Principal Officer Adnan Ash Shafique, FAVP Monirul Haque, Senior Officer (SO) Rifat-ul Mursalin, Officer Saifur Rahman and SO Shahinur Rahman.

During the inspection, the officials were asked to explain the transactions in their accounts.

Except for Saleh Ahmed, who was on leave due to illness, the officials told the inspection team that they had handed over their signed cheques to the marketing department on the advice of the bank’s management, the BB report showed.

“They said the money was intended to cover expenses such as transportation, hospitality and gifts related to bringing in deposits under the bank’s 2026 deposit campaign.”

The managing director told the inspection team that the bank had secured a Tk 100 crore deposit from Gazipur City Corporation through the Ujjibon campaign at an interest rate of 2.5 percent, according to the report.

He claimed that additional expenses were incurred for business development and hospitality to bring in the deposit, taking the effective cost of the deposit to 6.5 percent.

As the interest rate on a one-year fixed deposit was around 11.5 percent, the bank would save about 5 percentage points through the arrangement, he informed the inspection team, according to the BB report.

The Daily Star tried to reach Md Obaidul Hoque, managing director of the bank, for comment over the phone and through WhatsApp text messages, but he did not respond to the phone calls or messages until the report was filed.

Bangladesh Bank, however, found that the expenses were improperly routed through the personal bank accounts of 13 officials and paid as incentives without approval from the board.
Author: Star Business Report

Title: Internet banking transactions rise 6.22% in June
Content:
The value of internet banking transactions in Bangladesh grew by 6.22 percent month-on-month to Tk 1.84 lakh crore in June 2026, driven mainly by sharp increases in two payment systems, according to a recent central bank report.

The total had stood at Tk 1.73 lakh crore in May 2026.

The transactional values of Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) and National Payment Switch Bangladesh (NPSB) rose while Bangladesh Electronic Fund Transfer Network (BEFTN) fell, according to the e-Banking and e-Commerce Statistics review by Bangladesh Bank (BB).

RTGS, NPSB and BEFTN are BB-operated interbank payment systems, but they serve different purposes.

BEFTN is for scheduled batch transfers, NPSB is for real-time card and account transactions, and RTGS is for high-value, instant gross settlement-- all three route transactions among the country's scheduled banks and mobile financial service providers.

Among the individual channels, RTGS transactions rose 26.09 percent to Tk 50,461 crore in June, up from Tk 40,022 crore in May.

NPSB transactions increased 2.70 percent to Tk 57,480 crore in June from Tk 55,967 crore in May, the report showed.

BEFTN transfers, by contrast, declined to Tk 11,638 crore in June from Tk 12,987 crore in May. “It is clear that a large number of customers are using internet banking to access financial services,” BB said in the report.

However, the total number of internet banking customers fell slightly during the same period, decreasing 0.64 percent to 2.27 crore in June from 2.28 crore in May.

The data also showed that among the internet banking customer base, 1.78 crore were male, 44 lakh were female, and 4.7 lakh were registered under "other" in June.

As of June, 58 scheduled banks were offering internet banking services in the country.
Author: Star Business Report

Title: 7,896 customers withdraw Tk 327 crore on second day
Content:
Some 7,896 customers of the five merged banks withdrew Tk 327 crore on the second day of fund disbursement, officials of Sammilito Islami Bank said.

The bank, formed last year through the merger of five troubled Islamic banks—First Security Islami, Global Islami, Union, Exim and Social Islami—started repaying depositors on September 7.

Depositors of the five had been struggling to withdraw their money for more than two years and staged protests demanding the return of their deposits.

In addition, around 12,000 new customers applied to withdraw Tk 331 crore today, the officials said.

Abedur Rahman Sikder, managing director and chief executive officer of Sammilito Islami Bank, told The Daily Star that around 19,000 customers had applied to withdraw more than Tk 1,000 crore, but they had withdrawn only a small portion of the amount because they have confidence in the bank.

On August 25, Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman announced that individual depositors would be allowed to withdraw the principal amount of their deposits according to their needs from September 1.

Following the announcement, Sammilito Islami began accepting applications from customers and continued the process.

Bangladesh Bank provided Tk 5,000 crore on Sunday to facilitate payments to customers of the five banks.

Sikder said the bank had contacted all customers who had applied to withdraw money and asked them to come to their respective branches.

“Not everyone came to withdraw their money,” he said.
Author: Star Business Report

Title: Banks asked to verify certificates of all officers in 7 months
Content:
Bangladesh Bank has asked all scheduled banks to verify the educational certificates of their officers and employees within seven months, following repeated cases of questionable recruitment and forged qualifications across the banking sector.

BB issued a circular in this regard today.

Under the new directive, banks must complete verification of the academic credentials of all existing employees by March 31, 2027.

All new recruitment must be made through competitive examinations and interviews.

For new recruits, the latest educational certificate must be verified within one year of joining.

The central bank has also tightened recruitment procedures, requiring banks to publicly advertise entry-level vacancies and select candidates through competitive examinations and interviews.

The move comes amid allegations that some banks have recruited employees without properly examining educational certificates, assessing qualifications, or following transparent recruitment procedures.

In some cases, employees allegedly secured jobs through personal references or other informal channels without a public job circular or competitive examination.

BB asked banks to publish vacancies for entry-level positions such as management trainee officer, senior officer, probationary officer, junior officer, and trainee cash officer on their websites or job portals and in at least two national newspapers.

Candidates for such posts must go through a written or online test followed by an interview, and the bank must appoint candidates based on the competitive process.

For senior employees recruited from another bank or financial institution, at least an interview will be mandatory.

If a bank recruits a senior employee from another bank, it may rely on the previous employer's verification only if the release order clearly identifies the certificates that were checked. Otherwise, the recruiting bank must conduct its own verification.

The requirements appear particularly significant against allegations of non-transparent recruitment in several banks. The problem is not new.

The new rules require each bank to verify an employee's latest academic certificate directly with the issuing university, education board, or other relevant authority.

Any certificate submitted later for promotion, confirmation, or other employment benefits must likewise be verified, and the verification record kept in the employee's personal file.

If a certificate is found to be fake, the bank must take disciplinary or administrative action and record the case in the Corporate Memory Management System.

The CMMS shared system was introduced by Bangladesh Bank in 2019 to prevent employees removed from one bank for misconduct from obtaining employment at another bank without disclosure.

Alongside the recruitment and certificate-verification requirements, Bangladesh Bank has ordered banks to formulate or update comprehensive human resources policies covering recruitment, probation, training, performance assessment, promotion, transfers, succession planning, termination, leave, code of conduct, conflict of interest, whistleblower protection, grievances, disciplinary procedures, and anti-harassment measures.

The respective bank boards must adopt the updated HR policies by March 31, 2027.
Author: Star Business Report

Title: Govt eyes 2-3% GDP contribution from creative economy: Khosru
Content:
Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury today said the government is working to raise the contribution of the creative economy to 2 to 3 percent of the country’s gross domestic product (GDP).

Utilising the potential of this sector would generate widespread employment, boost foreign exchange earnings, and unlock new economic opportunities, he said at an event organised by Karmasangsthan Bank at the Osmani Memorial Auditorium in Dhaka.

The state bank launched the ‘Small Business and Micro-Entrepreneur Financing Fund’ (SBMEF) at the programme.

Highlighting global trends, Khosru said the creative economy accounts for up to 10 percent of GDP—the final value of goods and services produced in an economy over a certain period—in several countries.

He said that Bangladesh’s culinary heritage, music, culture, theatre, film, and online-based creative outputs have strong potential in global markets.

While extensive creative work takes place across rural areas, it has remained largely unmonetised. With targeted support, these creative endeavours can be transformed into marketable products, he added.

Underlining the promise of IT professionals and freelancers, the minister emphasised adding value to their work to make it competitive nationally and internationally.

Khosru cited Thailand's "One Village, One Product" initiative and said home-based rural production was integrated into global supply chains in the Southeast Asian country through government assistance in raw material sourcing, skill development, design, and branding.

A similar support framework can be implemented in Bangladesh, he said.

Under the SBMEF, the government has allocated Tk 50 crore for the pilot phase and is expected to provide more based on the success of the pilot phase.

Finance Secretary Md Khairuzzaman Mozumder said loans under the scheme would carry an interest rate of 5 to 6 percent—significantly lower than standard microcredit rates, which typically range between 24 and 25 percent.

Financial Institutions Division Secretary Nazma Mobarek said the initiative directly aligns with national employment objectives, particularly targeting the high unemployment rate among youth aged 15 to 30.

Loans disbursed via Karmasangsthan Bank will help build youth entrepreneurship, initially rolling out across three districts before expanding nationwide, she added.

Karmasangsthan Bank Managing Director Arun Kumar Chowdhury said it has a target to create employment for 900,000 unemployed individuals over the next five years, aligning with the government’s goal of generating ten million jobs in the country during the same period.

Karmasangsthan Bank aims to disburse 50 percent of the loans from the fund to women entrepreneurs.
Author: Star Business Report

Title: Hajj-2027 registration ends on Sept 24
Content:
The registration process for the 2027 Hajj will end on September 24 this year, with no scope for an extension, according to a notification issued by the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

As per instructions from the Saudi government, immediately after the registration process ends, the final number of Hajj pilgrims from Bangladesh will be communicated to the Saudi authorities.

Based on the final number of pilgrims, necessary activities, including remittance of funds for the Saudi phase, medical checkups, fitness certificates, vaccination, and training programs, will be carried out.

Bangladesh’s Hajj quota for 2027 is 78,500 pilgrims. As of September 9, 2026, a total of 3,741 pilgrims have registered, including 1,065 through the government channel and 2,676 through the private channel.

All concerned have been requested to complete registration within the stipulated deadline of September 24 to ensure their participation in the 2027 Hajj in accordance with the instructions of the Saudi government.

The registration process for Hajj 2027 began on July 27 this year.
Author: BSS

Title: State Minister Tuku: Dengue crisis may worsen in coming months
Content:
State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salauddin Tuku has said the ongoing dengue situation in Dhaka and other districts could take a more alarming turn over the coming months, urging citizens to remain vigilant from now.

"The risk of dengue may increase further in the coming months, so everyone needs to become aware from now," Tuku said while addressing a views exchange meeting with lawmakers and administration on the overall law and order situation and development activities in Dhaka district, held at the Dhaka Deputy Commissioner's conference room.

The state minister said public representatives, the administration and local residents must work together to combat dengue through cleanliness drives, destruction of mosquito breeding grounds and heightened public awareness.

On law and order in the capital, Tuku said maintaining law and order is not the administration's responsibility alone.

A safe and stable society, he said, can only be built through the coordinated efforts of political leadership, the administration, law enforcement agencies and the general public.

Noting that the government is working to keep the country's law and order situation normal while advancing development activities, he called for effective coordination among the district administration, police administration and public representatives, adding that obstacles to development work must be identified and addressed alongside maintaining law and order.

He stressed the need for special surveillance to prevent various criminal activities in the capital and its surrounding areas, particularly in crime-prone zones, calling for increased law enforcement activity and greater political and social awareness in those areas.

Describing drugs as a major threat to society that is drawing in people from all walks of life, Tuku said the administration, public representatives and social organisations must play a more active role in curbing the spread of narcotics.

Addressing government officials, the state minister said that as state functionaries, they must carry out their duties giving top priority to public welfare and state interests, stressing that all administrative activities should be conducted in the interest of the state and the people, not any individual or group.

The meeting was chaired by Dhaka Deputy Commissioner Farida Khanom. State Minister for the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain attended as special guest.

Also present were Chief Whip of the Opposition Nahid Islam, Dhaka-12 MP Saiful Alam Khan Milon, reserved women's seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed, Superintendent of Police Shamima Parveen, representatives of various law enforcement agencies, local government officials, public representatives and members of the district law and order committee.
Author: UNB

Title: Gopalganj university library struggles with books, space, technology
Content:
A shortage of academic and reference books, inadequate seating, slow internet and a lack of modern technological facilities are hampering study and research at the central library of Gopalganj Science and Technology University (GSTU).

The library, established in 2014, has 36,152 books, including academic publications, Liberation War-related books, fiction and novels. It also has around 1,500 printed journals and 500 magazines.

Despite the collection, students say the library lacks many course-specific and specialised books needed for their studies. It also does not have adequate access to international journals, e-books or modern digital facilities. An anti-plagiarism software system for teachers has yet to be introduced, while students do not have computers for academic use.

As a result, students say the library is yet to become an effective centre for higher education, research and knowledge practice.

A visit to the library found several air conditioners and fans out of order. There are also not enough desks for students, while chairs are placed so close together that users have to move them to get in and out. The movement creates noise that can be heard across the reading room, disrupting study.

Students have demanded high-speed internet, books according to their academic needs, a job corner and modernisation of the library.

Alamgir Hossain, a student of the 2018-19 academic session in the Department of Bangla, said around 9,320 students are currently studying at the university, while the library has seating capacity for only about 200.

“The student-to-seat ratio is around 1:50. There are not enough seats. Besides, the internet is slow and there is a shortage of necessary books. Noise from the surrounding areas also disrupts our studies,” he said.

Tamin Iqbal, a student of the 2019-20 academic session, said the library should serve as a centre for higher education, research and knowledge practice, but the existing facilities prevent it from playing that role.

“The number of students has increased, but the number of seats has not. The seating capacity must be increased. We also need high-speed internet. We hope the authorities will resolve these problems quickly,” he said.

Yaminur Rahman Arik, a student of the 2021-22 academic session, said the library lacked adequate subject-specific and reference books.

“Students come here to find books that are unavailable in the hall libraries, but often we cannot find them. There are also not enough reference books. The library does not provide enough scope for developing our knowledge and intellect through study,” he said.

“As a result, many students are frustrated and have become reluctant to use the library. We hope it will be turned into a proper centre for higher education, research and knowledge practice,” he added.

Acting Librarian Nasirul Islam said the library building has two floors, although it was originally planned as a four-storey facility.

“We are facing problems because of space and staff shortages. There is no automation system either, so we have to perform our work manually,” he said.

The library remains open from 9am to 10pm every day, he said, adding that staff members have to work in 13 shifts a week, putting additional pressure on them.

“Despite this, we are trying to provide the best possible services to students. The new vice-chancellor has discussed modernising and expanding the library with us and has assured us that he will work to resolve its problems,” Nasirul said.

Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Md Sohel Hasan, who was appointed on August 25, said he was aware of the problems facing the library.

“I have heard about the problems of the library. We will take initiatives to make it more up-to-date by adding reference books on various subjects, international research journals and reliable sources of information beyond textbooks,” he said.

“We want to create a library that will help teachers and students contribute more effectively to education and research. It will also be developed in a way that helps students prepare for competitive examinations, including the BCS,” the vice-chancellor added.
Author: Monoj Kumar Saha

Title: Boat race draws thousands to Titas River after two-year hiatus
Content:
Thousands of spectators lined both banks of the Titas River in Brahmanbaria on Sunday as a colourful traditional boat race returned after a two-year hiatus.

Organised by the district administration, the race began at around 3:30pm along the stretch between Shimrailkandi and Medda areas of the district town.

Nine boats from different parts of Brahmanbaria took part in the competition, with the boat of Shapla Boys Club from Khamtapur village in Sadar upazila emerging as the winner.

Spectators began gathering along the riverbanks before noon, with the crowd swelling as the race drew closer. Once the competition began, cheers and chants from the packed riverbanks created a festive atmosphere.

The brightly decorated boats raced through the Titas as rowers paddled in unison, drawing loud cheers from supporters.

The last boat race on the Titas was held in 2023. The event is considered an important part of Brahmanbaria’s cultural heritage and traditionally attracts visitors from neighbouring districts.

Roni Alam, an expatriate living in Italy, travelled from Dhaka to watch the race.

“Boat racing is a festival close to our hearts. I came from Dhaka this morning despite the difficulties just to watch it. Seeing the enthusiasm of people on both banks has erased all my fatigue,” he said.

Another spectator, Al Amin Shaheen, said the event had created a festive atmosphere across the district.

“We want the boat race to be organised every year,” he said.

Brahmanbaria Deputy Commissioner Md Abusaid said the boat race was a popular traditional event.

“Boat racing is a festival close to the hearts of the people here. From next year, we will organise it on an even larger scale,” he said.

Brahmanbaria-3 MP Khaled Hossain Mahbub said the event highlighted the district’s cultural heritage amid what he described as recent negative campaigns about Brahmanbaria and its culture on social media.

“This boat race has shown that Brahmanbaria is a cultural capital. Boat racing is an integral part of our heritage,” he said, adding that he hoped the event would be organised regularly from next year.

Prizes were later handed over to the winning team at a ceremony attended by District Council Administrator Sirajul Islam, Deputy Director of the Local Government Division Shariful Islam, Superintendent of Police Shah Md Abdur Rouf, Additional Deputy Commissioner Ranjan Chandra Dey and other officials and local political leaders.
Author: Ujjal Kumar Chakraborty

Title: Fertiliser crunch fuels anger among Bhurungamari farmers
Content:
Growing demand for fertiliser during the peak Aman season and ahead of early winter vegetable cultivation is fuelling frustration among farmers in Bhurungamari upazila of Kurigram, with many saying they are struggling to obtain supplies from authorised dealers.

The growing discontent has already spilled into protests, road blockades and incidents involving fertiliser dealers, reflecting mounting tensions over distribution.

Farmers also complain that they receive little field-level advice from agriculture officials on which fertiliser or pesticide to use, and in what quantities.

Agriculture officials, however, say there is no overall shortage of fertiliser in the upazila. They blame excessive use and stockpiling by some farmers for putting additional pressure on supplies.

A visit to several unions on Thursday found farmers moving from one sales outlet to another in search of fertiliser. Many said they either failed to get supplies or received much less than they needed.

At 9am, farmers were seen waiting at the BCIC dealer outlet of Messrs Janarddan Chandra Saha at Camp Mor in Bangasonahat Union. Three to five farmers were reportedly sharing one sack of DAP, while urea distribution had been suspended because of insufficient stock.

The farmers said their Aman paddy was around one-and-a-half to nearly two months old and they wanted to apply fertiliser to the fields. Agriculture officials, however, said DAP was not needed at this stage and applying it would be wasteful.

Mohammad Ali and Abdul Aziz, who had collected DAP, said they were unaware that the fertiliser was not recommended for Aman paddy at this stage.

“We do not know which fertiliser should be applied and when. We look at the condition of the plants and apply fertiliser accordingly,” Mohammad Ali said.

Abdul Aziz, who has two bighas of Aman, said he could not obtain urea and was therefore planning to use DAP instead.

“I do not know what else to do. I am using DAP because I could not get urea,” he said.

Abul Hashem, a representative of the dealer, said demand had increased sharply as farmers had begun cultivating eggplant on hundreds of bighas of land in the char areas.

“The demand for fertiliser is very high, but we are not getting enough to meet it,” he said.

In Gunaiyer Kuti char along the Dudhkumar River, farmers were cultivating early-season eggplant on hundreds of bighas of land.

Several farmers said they needed urea and DAP but could not obtain enough. They also complained that block supervisors, or BSs, rarely visit their fields to provide advice.

Instead, representatives of private agrochemical companies often visit the area, and farmers rely on their recommendations, they said.

Hridoy Molla, who has cultivated eggplant on four bighas, said he was unable to obtain fertiliser according to his requirements.

“I am mixing organic fertiliser and magnesium and applying them to the fields. The BSs do not come here. We apply fertiliser based on the condition of the plants,” he said.

Another farmer, Ramadan Ali, said he was also forced to rely on his own experience.

“We do not get fertiliser or advice. No BS comes here. We use our own knowledge to decide what fertiliser and pesticides to apply,” he said.

Kurigram Department of Agricultural Extension Deputy Director Abdullah Al Mamun denied that agriculture officials were disconnected from farmers, but acknowledged that staff shortages made it difficult to reach everyone.

“There is a tendency among farmers in Bhurungamari to apply excessive amounts of fertiliser. Many are seeking fertiliser even when it is not necessary and do not follow the recommended doses,” he said.

“There is no need to apply DAP to Aman paddy at this stage. Doing so would be a waste. After September 20, there will also be no need to apply urea. Many farmers use DAP instead of urea,” he added.

Regarding the farmers’ complaints about a lack of field-level advice, Mamun said BSs were required to visit fields and provide technical support through field days and other programmes.

“There are many farmers in each union, while we have a shortage of manpower. So it may not always be possible to reach everyone. However, BSs are stationed at every union parishad, and farmers can go there for advice whenever necessary,” he said.

Considering the increased demand, the agriculture department has sought an additional allocation of 300 tonnes each of urea and DAP for Bhurungamari, beyond the upazila’s regular allocation, Mamun said.
Author: Ariful Islam Rigan

Title: IGP: Police must enhance skills, capacity to combat cybercrime
Content:
Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir on Sunday said there is no alternative to enhancing the skills and capacity of police personnel to combat cybercrime.

He made the remarks while inaugurating a 10-day Training of Trainers (ToT) course on investigation of cybercrime cases at the Police Staff College Bangladesh in Mirpur in Dhaka on Sunday.

“Artificial intelligence, deepfakes, encrypted communication systems and cloud computing have opened new avenues of opportunities, but at the same time created new challenges for law enforcement agencies,” the IGP said.

He said criminals are abusing technology to commit cyber-based fraud, online financial crimes, data theft, hacking, online harassment and digital extortion.

“Changes in the nature of policing have become a demand of the time to tackle the growing cybercrime. Developing investigation capacity to combat cybercrime is extremely essential for modern policing,” he said.

Addressing the police officers attending the training, the IGP said the course would help them acquire not only technical skills but also training and communication skills.

“The knowledge and skills gained through the training must be disseminated among other investigators,” he said, adding that effective training of other investigators would multiply the number of cybercrime case investigators.

The IGP thanked the Training Wing of Police Headquarters and the Police Staff College Bangladesh for arranging the timely training and stressed the need for regularly organising such training and updating training materials and modules.

Police Staff College Bangladesh Rector and Additional IGP Kazi Md Fazlul Karim presided over the programme, while CID chief and Additional IGP Barrister Mohammad Mosharraf Hossain attended as a special guest.

DIG (Training) Md Ekramul Habib delivered the welcome address, while Additional DIG (Training-2) Dr Mosammat Shehela Parveen presented the roadmap and implementation strategy for cybercrime investigation training.

Faculty members and resource persons of Police Staff College Bangladesh were also present.

The Police Staff College Bangladesh organised the 10-day course at the initiative of the Training Branch of Police Headquarters.

A total of 332 police officers participating in the ToT course will, in phases, provide training to field-level investigators of cybercrime cases.
Author: UNB

Title: ASK condemns rape of two dancers hired for wedding event
Content:
Two women dancers were allegedly gang-raped on the Titas River in Sarail, Brahmanbaria, after being hired to perform at a wedding, Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK) said.

In a statement on Sunday, the rights group condemned the incident and expressed deep concern and outrage.

ASK said the two women were taken aboard a boat on September 11 on the pretext of performing at an event. They were allegedly held hostage at gunpoint and raped for an extended period.

The incident is a grave violation of the women’s safety and dignity and a serious assault on their professional rights and freedom to work, ASK said.

A woman has the fundamental right to pursue her chosen profession with dignity and work in a safe environment, it said. Working as a dancer or performing at an event for payment must not expose anyone to violence or abuse, ASK added.

The organisation said every citizen has the right to work safely, and ensuring such safety is the state’s responsibility.

ASK said the incident should not be viewed merely as a brutal crime committed by a few individuals. It also raises serious questions about the effectiveness of state mechanisms to prevent violence against women, law enforcement, and ensuring women’s safety while travelling and working. ASK demanded the immediate arrest of all those involved and their prosecution following an impartial and professional investigation. It also called for ensuring that no perpetrator escapes justice due to influence or pressure.

The organisation also demanded security, necessary medical treatment, psychological and legal support for the victims, as well as protection of their identities and privacy.

“Women’s safety is not merely a law-and-order issue; it is a question of equal rights, dignity and human rights,” ASK said, stressing that the state must ensure an environment where women can pursue their chosen professions without fear or insecurity.
Author: Tribune Report

Title: Know groups and schedule as Bangladesh begin Asian Games women’s football campaign Monday
Content:
Bangladesh will take part in the Asian Games women’s football competition for the second time after making their debut in the previous edition in China.

The Bengal Tigresses will begin their 2026 Asian Games campaign against Asian powerhouse North Korea at Nagai Stadium in Osaka on Monday.

They will then face another Asian giant, South Korea, at the same venue in their second group-stage match.

The 20th edition of the continental multi-sport competition is being held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with football matches taking place across several Japanese cities.

The women’s football competition will be staged in Osaka, Fukuroi, Gifu and Kariya, while the men’s event will be played in Osaka, Toyota, Nagoya and Kariya.

At the last Asian Games in 2023, Japan won the women’s football gold medal in Hangzhou, while the Republic of Korea clinched the men’s title.

The 12-team women’s competition, divided into three groups, will run from September 14 to October 2. The men’s competition, featuring 15 teams following Iraq’s withdrawal, will take place from September 15 to October 3.

Bangladesh have been drawn in Group F alongside the Republic of Korea, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea and Myanmar.

The women in red and green, who made history by qualifying for the final round of the AFC Women’s Asian Cup 2026 in Australia in March, suffered an injury setback ahead of their Asian Games opener.

Defender Nabiran Khatun has been ruled out of the squad after sustaining a knee injury during a practice match in China last week.

Bangladesh head coach Peter Butler said the team’s strength lies in the players’ fighting mentality as they prepare for a challenging group stage.

Group E: Japan, Chinese Taipei, Vietnam, Thailand Group F: South Korea, North Korea, Bangladesh, Myanmar Group G: People’s Republic of China, Philippines, Uzbekistan, Hong Kong, China

Author: Tribune Report

Title: Dengue: Six die; 1,561 hospitalized in 24hrs
Content:
Six people died of dengue, and 1,561 new patients were hospitalized across the country in the 24 hours until 8am on Sunday.

With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 149 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

The new deaths were reported in Dhaka, Chittagong, Khulna and Mymensingh divisions, it said.

Since January 1 this year, hospitals across the country have admitted a total of 51,837 dengue patients.

Of them, 48,093 have been discharged after recovery, according to the DGHS.
Author: UNB

Title: Maulana Faruki murder: Charge framing hearing deferred to Oct 25
Content:
A Dhaka court on Sunday deferred until October 25 the hearing on framing charges in the murder and robbery case over the killing of Maulana Nurul Islam Faruki 12 years ago.

The case was scheduled for a hearing on charge framing before Dhaka Ninth Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Mahmudul Islam. However, lawyer Md Zayedur Rahman, representing accused Engineer alias Riaz alias Ripon, sought time, saying the accused could not appear in court because his mobile phone was switched off.

The court granted the time petition and fixed October 25 for the next hearing, said bench assistant Abul Kashem.

Abdullah Al Tasnim Nahid and Abu Raihan Mahmud Abdul Hadi appeared in court on Sunday. Hadisur Rahman Sagar was produced before the court from jail.

Advocate K M Shariful Islam, representing Sagar, filed a bail petition. The court also fixed Oct 25 for a hearing on the application.

Meanwhile, 2 accused, Mahmud Ibn Bashar and Rafiqul Islam Fardin, remain absconding, and arrest warrants have been issued against them. Mahmud Ibn Bashar is also on bail.

On August 27, 2014, unidentified assailants hacked and slit the throat of Maulana Nurul Islam Faruki at his residence in East Rajabazar. His son, Faisal Faruki, filed a case over the incident.

On November 5, 2024, Criminal Investigation Department (CID) Additional Special Police Superintendent K M Abul Kashem, the investigating officer, submitted a charge sheet against 6 people, 10 years after the incident. Although the case was filed over the murder, the CID investigation also found allegations of robbery against the accused.

According to the case details, the incident took place at around 9pm on August 27, 2014, at Faruki’s residence in East Rajabazar. Police recovered his body later that night.

According to the First Information Report (FIR), at around 7pm on the day of the incident, several people rang the doorbell of Nurul Islam Faruki’s residence. After the door was opened, 2 men entered and sat with Nurul Islam in the drawing room.

Shortly afterward, another 6–7 people entered the residence. As there was not enough space to sit, Maruf Hossain, a maternal cousin of Faisal Faruki, went inside to bring chairs.

When he returned, he saw the accused holding a pistol and a machete to Nurul Islam’s head. They then tied up everyone at the residence and killed Nurul Islam Faruki.

The assailants took cash, mobile phones, gold jewelry and a camera from the residence.
Author: Tribune Report

Title: The succession question returns to haunt Awami League
Content:
A name has suddenly surfaced across Bangladeshi social media and various established media outlets, a name well known in political circles but one that had not been mentioned publicly for quite some time.

Sheikh Fazlul Karim Selim has not only returned to the spotlight, but his name has also sparked a genuine debate both within and outside his party.

This debate was initiated by Sheikh Hasina herself.

In a telephonic interview with the Indian online news portal The Wall, Hasina remarked that Sheikh Selim could assume responsibility for the party in her absence.

Although she described this as a temporary measure in accordance with the party’s constitution, many interpreted it as a sign that she had chosen Sheikh Selim as her successor.

This assumption gave rise to various speculations, such as the idea that Sheikh Hasina was stepping away from politics or retiring, or that she had realized a return to Dhaka was no longer possible and was therefore handing over responsibility to Sheikh Selim.

The actual context, however, was different.

Amal Sarkar, executive editor of The Wall, had raised the issue during the interview. He asked who would take charge of the party if Sheikh Hasina were to be imprisoned or taken into custody by an agency for interrogation upon her return to Dhaka.

In response, Sheikh Hasina explained the Awami League’s constitution, stating that the most senior member of the Presidium would assume responsibility in such a scenario.

Currently, of the 16 Presidium members, three have passed away, six are in prison, one’s whereabouts are unknown, and six remain active. Among them, Sheikh Selim is the most senior.

The explanation is clear. A similar situation arose during the 2007-08 “1/11” government era when Sheikh Hasina was imprisoned.

At the time, senior Presidium member Zillur Rahman took charge. That did not mean he had been designated as Hasina’s successor to the party presidency.

While the matter appears straightforward, there is no doubt that the mention of Sheikh Selim’s name fuelled the subsequent rumours and speculation.

Sheikh Selim has been elected to the National Parliament nine times. This fact alone sends a clear message about his popularity and local influence in Gopalganj.

He is the nephew of Bangladesh’s founding leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, specifically, Sheikh Hasina’s paternal cousin.

Perhaps because of this close familial relationship, many view Sheikh Selim not merely as someone who could take “temporary charge,” but as a potential permanent successor. That is precisely where the complication lies.

A Dhaka-based news portal has already reported that several senior leaders currently in Kolkata held a meeting and expressed disagreement with Hasina’s decision.

The report further stated that they proposed Jahangir Kabir Nanak for the role.

The issue here is that some observers have questioned the credibility of the report, even raising doubts about whether such a meeting actually took place.

Regardless, one thing is clear: There is no unanimous support for Sheikh Selim among Awami League leaders and activists.

Many perceive him as the kind of leader who “disappears during times of crisis.” And this is not merely about Sheikh Selim; the episode signals a deepening crisis within the Awami League.

The reported meeting is merely an indication of how acute the infighting among the party’s leaders in exile has become.

Ever since Sheikh Hasina’s tenure began, this question has been raised repeatedly, yet no satisfactory answer has ever emerged.

Who comes after Sheikh Hasina? Who will take the helm of the Awami League if Hasina retires? Does she have any plans regarding succession?

There has never been a direct answer to these questions.

Whenever confronted with this question, Hasina would say that the party would decide who its leader should be.

However, no one considered the possibility that the party might not be in a position to make such a decision when the time came.

By closing off the path to a transfer of power through elections, the Awami League perhaps believed it could safely remain in power for the long haul.

Yet, having enjoyed the comforts of governance for so long, the party, once a force that shook the streets, forgot that there are far more perilous paths to a change of power than elections.

It was precisely through such a perilous path that it was forced to relinquish power in 2024.

Since the fall of the Awami League, the question has resurfaced: Is a change in leadership on the horizon? How exactly will it happen, and who will step in?

Various people have attempted to answer these questions in different ways.

Many had assumed that the Awami League would be restructured around members against whom there were no allegations of serious crimes.

However, it became evident that even if a leader faced no such accusations at the time, the very moment they began the task of reorganizing the party, their name could be implicated in a case involving murder or “crimes against humanity.”

Yet, talk began circulating about a so-called “refined” or “reformed” Awami League. Names such as Saber Hossain Chowdhury, Shirin Sharmin Chaudhury, and even Narayanganj Mayor Selina Hayat Ivy were linked to this idea, although none of them publicly spoke of playing a role in restructuring the party.

However, one thing became clear: Regardless of the extent to which former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina bears responsibility for the Awami League’s current plight, in the eyes of the party’s grassroots activists, there is no leader other than her.

If the party were to be restructured under someone else’s leadership, it might remain a political party, but it would certainly cease to be the Awami League as they know it.

On the other hand, conversations with Awami League members, including former members of Parliament, over the past year or so suggest that if Sheikh Hasina herself were to initiate a transition process and select a successor, the rank and file might well accept that new leadership.

Yet there is another complication.

Over the last five decades, Bangladesh’s two major parties, the Awami League and the BNP, have become excessively dependent on particular families.

The BNP has never managed to step out of the shadow of its founder, Ziaur Rahman, nor has it made any serious attempt to do so.

The party is well aware that without the umbrella of the Zia family, its unity could crumble.

To keep the party together, leadership passed from General Zia to his wife, Khaleda Zia, and subsequently to their son, Tarique Rahman.

The situation within the Awami League is somewhat different.

Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was not the party’s founder; the Awami League was established by Maulana Abdul Hamid Khan Bhashani and Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy.

However, under Sheikh Mujib’s leadership, the Awami League became the embodiment of the hopes and aspirations of the Bengali people in what was then East Pakistan.

It was under Sheikh Mujib that the party spearheaded the movement for self-determination and contested the 1970 elections. He provided the direction for the independence movement in March 1971, and the subsequent Liberation War was fought in his name.

Because of this historical continuity, and the fact that Mujib and almost his entire family were killed on August 15, 1975, the Awami League became inextricably linked with the Sheikh family.

Despite the presence of prominent leaders within the party following Mujib’s assassination, they brought Sheikh Hasina back from exile in 1981 to take the helm.

It would come as no surprise if, during these difficult times for the Awami League, party leaders and activists once again looked towards the Sheikh family.

A parallel can be drawn with the BNP, where party members naturally accepted Khaleda Zia’s son, Tarique Rahman, as her successor.

Whether it is a matter of temporary responsibility or long-term succession, there is no doubt that the Awami League must contemplate its post-Hasina future.

At the same time, however, it must address how to regain public trust following 2024.

There appear to be two clear reasons for the party’s current organizational stagnation and crisis of morale.

First is the issue of leadership. Despite the continued faith in Sheikh Hasina, the Awami League is currently, effectively, leaderless.

Whether because of the ban on its activities, the imprisonment or flight abroad of many leaders, or the looming threat of legal cases hanging over many, the bottom line is that the party faces an acute leadership crisis.

Second, the Awami League has failed to come to terms with the events of 2024, even after two years. There appears to have been no internal self-criticism or even a meaningful process of introspection within the party.

Its leaders remain fixated on conspiracy theories and continue to deny their own culpability.

The Awami League needs to ask itself some critical questions:

Why did the movement to oust the government occur?

Why did a movement become necessary to bring about a change in government?

Why did students repeatedly take to the streets?

Why did the urban middle class support the movement?

Why did so many people lose their lives?

The answers to these questions will determine the message the party conveys to the public.

If the Awami League views itself as a party of the people, it must be accountable to them.

It is through this process of accountability that the party’s future leadership may become clear.

Sabir Mustafa is the former head of BBC Bangla and is currently working as a freelance journalist and podcaster.
Author: Sabir Mustafa

Title: Harun’s family receives PM’s gift 12 years after his death
Content:
More than 12 years after Jubo Dal leader Mohammad Harunur Rashid was killed in police firing in Feni, his family has finally received a new home.

BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi handed over the keys to the newly built house to Harunur’s family at Jagatjibanpur in Farhadnagar Union of the district on Sunday. His wife, Bibi Zohra, daughter Majeda Akter and son Touhidul Islam received the keys.

According to district BNP sources, Harunur was killed in police firing on December 4, 2013, amid tensions surrounding a BNP-led programme in support of a hartal on Shaheed Shahidullah Kaiser Road in Feni town. He was then vice-president of the Farhadnagar Union Jubo Dal.

After his death, his wife and children endured years of hardship, including uncertainty over their livelihood and housing.

The new house was built in Jagatjibanpur under an initiative of “Amra BNP Poribar” to rehabilitate the family, following instructions from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. Construction began on April 12.

Speaking at the key handover ceremony, Ruhul Kabir Rizvi accused the previous Awami League government of enforced disappearances and killings.

“Sheikh Hasina did not hesitate to kill anyone to consolidate power. Enforced disappearances and killings continued for 17 years,” he said.

Local BNP leaders recalled Harunur’s political contributions and pledged to continue supporting his family.

The family expressed relief after finally receiving a secure home following years of housing difficulties, though the loss of their husband and father continues to leave a deep void in their lives.

After the ceremony, Rizvi visited Harunur’s grave and inaugurated the nameplate of the new house.
Author: Tribune Report

Title: 'The Difficult Bride' wins independent critics’ award at Venice
Content:
Bangladeshi filmmaker Rubaiyat Hossain’s “The Difficult Bride” has won the Independent Film Critics Award, Premio Bisato d’Oro, at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival ahead of the festival’s official awards ceremony.

The recognition adds to a landmark year for the film, which made history as the first Bangladeshi feature to compete in the Orizzonti Competition at the Venice Film Festival.

Set in contemporary Dhaka, “The Difficult Bride” follows Zaineen, a young bride-to-be whose body begins to transform as she undergoes beauty rituals and preparations for her wedding.

Blending feminist folk horror, body horror, and supernatural elements, the film examines how women’s bodies can become sites of family expectations, social control, and desire.

Hossain said the award was particularly meaningful because of the personal themes explored in the film.

“I made ‘The Difficult Bride’ from a very intimate place, thinking about the ways women learn to inhabit, discipline, and sometimes fear their own bodies,” she said. “To have the film recognized by independent critics in Venice is deeply meaningful to me.”

She added that she hopes the film will allow audiences to experience Bangladesh beyond its social realities through its folklore, imagination, darkness, and beauty.

The Bisato d’Oro is an independent critics’ prize associated with the Venice Film Festival and is separate from the official awards presented by the Biennale.

The film’s Venice selection had already attracted international attention, with critics highlighting its use of South Asian wedding rituals within a feminist folk-horror framework. IndieWire described the film as transforming South Asian wedding tropes into “feminist folk horror."

Produced by Francois D’Artemare, “The Difficult Bride” is an international co-production between Bangladesh, France, Germany, Norway, and Portugal. International sales are handled by Films Boutique.
Author: Showtime Desk

Title: UN: Nearly 86,000 flee fighting in Yemen
Content:
Flaring fighting between government forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has displaced nearly 86,000 people, the United Nations said Sunday, with the number surging by 10,000 from a day earlier.

Tens of thousands have taken flight in the wake of a week-long Houthi offensive that culminated in the group capturing the remainder of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and several strategic islands, cementing their hold on the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait.

“Displacement in Yemen, the Arab world’s poorest country, has now reached 85,818 people,” the International Organization for Migration said in a statement, a day after putting the number of people displaced since July at 76,000.

The UN agency stressed that more than 82,000 of those displaced had been forced to flee their homes since the start of September, when the Houthis, who have for years controlled large parts of northern Yemen, launched their large-scale offensive against Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces.

The displacements had happened across the west coast and Taiz areas, the IOM said.

Taiz was the hardest-hit, it said, with some 9,280 households, or nearly 56,000 people, displaced from districts in that province alone.

And now, some of those displaced have begun fleeing Yemen altogether, IOM said, pointing out that more than 2,000 people had reached Djibouti.

The UN body told AFP that the first arrivals landed on Thursday evening.

Djibouti lies opposite Yemen across the Bab al-Mandab strait, which has become an important artery for Saudi Arabian oil exports after Iran began its blockade on the Strait of Hormuz at the start of the Middle East war.

Those arriving in Djibouti -- many of them women and young children -- had been transported to a site in Obock where they were receiving assistance, IOM said, warning that “more are expected to flee as fighting intensifies.”

“Behind every number is a family who’s lost everything,” IOM chief Amy Pope said in the statement.

“Many have been displaced multiple times. People are crossing the sea with nothing because they have no other choice left,” she said.

Pope highlighted that Yemen was a “country torn by poverty and conflict, and it cannot carry this crisis alone.”

“I call on donors to scale up support now, for those arriving in Djibouti and for the communities in Obock receiving them.”
Author: AFP

Title: Non-tax revenue surges in Q4’FY26
Content:
Driven by a surge in dividend payouts from state-owned enterprises, interest earnings, and administrative fees, Bangladesh’s non-tax revenue (NTR) nearly tripled in the final quarter (April–June) of FY26.

Data from Bangladesh Bank shows that quarterly NTR collections leaped 195.3% quarter-on-quarter to Tk18,774 crore, up from Tk6,358 crore in Q3 FY26.

While the collection provided a temporary boost to overall public finances, total annual revenue receipts reached Tk476,000 crore—achieving 81.0% of the revised annual target of Tk588,000 crore.

Economists warn that heavy reliance on non-recurring state enterprise dividends fails to address underlying structural weaknesses in tax collection.

State-owned enterprise dividends served as the primary growth driver, generating Tk10,361 crore and accounting for 55.2% of total non-tax collections in Q4.

Revenue collected outside the National Board of Revenue (Non-NBR) rose 39.9% quarter-on-quarter to Tk2,000 crore, heavily driven by stamp duties.

"The sharp rise in non-tax revenue is encouraging on paper, but it does not indicate a sustainable improvement in the government's revenue mobilization capacity," noted Masrur Reaz, chairman of Policy Exchange Bangladesh.

"Non-NBR taxes remain one of the smallest components of state revenue, pointing to significant underutilized potential," Reaz added.

"Automating collection systems, improving regulatory compliance, and strengthening agency coordination can turn these fragmented streams into a diversified revenue pillar."
