Title: 'Shoot me dead instead of filing repeated cases': Misti Suvas breaks down in court
Content:
Misti Suvas, who was shown arrested in an attempted murder case filed with Ashulia Police Station, told a Dhaka court today (13 September), "Instead of filing cases against me again and again, shoot me dead."

She made the remarks during a hearing before Dhaka Senior Judicial Magistrate Md Tajul Islam Sohag this afternoon.

Musammat Simu Akter Brishti alias Misti Suvas was brought to the court from jail. Shortly after noon, she was taken from the detention cell to the dock, where she reportedly fell ill, became dizzy and collapsed.

Police personnel took her back to the detention cell. She was later brought to the dock again after recovering.

During the hearing, she sought the judge's permission to speak and said she had gone to the National Martyrs' Memorial to lay flowers as the daughter of a freedom fighter.

"That cannot be a crime. A deep conspiracy is being hatched against me. Whenever I get bail, another case is filed against me. I have done nothing wrong. Instead of filing cases against me again and again, shoot me dead," she said.

Defence lawyer Golam Rabbani urged the court not to show her arrested in the case.

However, after the hearing, the court ordered that Misti Suvas be shown arrested in the case and sent her to jail.

Misti Suvas was arrested on 26 March this year while travelling to the National Martyrs' Memorial to lay flowers. She was subsequently shown arrested in four cases and has remained in jail since then.

According to the case statement, teenager Md Abir joined the anti-discrimination student movement at Baipayl intersection in Ashulia on 5 August 2024.

During the protest, armed members of the Awami League, Jubo League and Chhatra League allegedly attacked the protesters. Abir was seriously injured after being shot.

A case was filed with Ashulia Police Station on 31 October 2024 over the incident.

Title: Strong local government essential to strengthening democracy: President
Content:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has said democracy must be institutionalised and that strengthening local government is essential to strengthening democracy.

He made the remarks when administrators of 33 district councils paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban this afternoon (13 September).

Describing local government as the biggest strength of democracy, the president instructed the district council administrators to remain active and vigilant in carrying out their responsibilities and work to overcome the corruption left behind by the fascist regime.

During the meeting, the district council administrators placed various demands before the president, including raising their status. In response, the president assured them that the government is a government of the people and that steps would be taken promptly to resolve their problems.

He said the government is attaching importance to strengthening the local government system to decentralise power.

The president also recalled with gratitude the active participation of the district council administrators in the movement to restore democracy and the long struggle against fascism.

He also gave the administrators necessary directives to accelerate development activities of the district councils, ensure citizen services at the local level and maintain administrative transparency.

Title: DSEX plunges 96 points as broad sell-off grips Dhaka bourse
Content:
The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) suffered a broad-based sell-off today (13 September), with the benchmark DSEX plunging 96 points as all major indices closed sharply lower.

The DSEX fell 1.75% to 5,418, its 96-point decline reflecting widespread selling pressure across the market.

The Shariah-compliant DSES index dropped 19 points, or 1.78%, to 1,085, while the blue-chip DS30 index lost 23 points, or 1.11%, to close at 2,072.

Trading activity remained substantial, with 182,186 transactions involving 23.65 crore shares. Total turnover stood at Tk571.32 crore.

Declining stocks overwhelmingly outnumbered gainers, with 336 issues ending lower, compared with just 27 that advanced.

Another 21 stocks remained unchanged.

Title: Chevron team meets PM, discusses investment in Bangladesh's gas sector
Content:
A high-level delegation from Chevron met Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today (13 September) and discussed the US energy giant's potential investment in Bangladesh's energy sector, particularly gas.

President of Chevron's Base Assets and Emerging Countries, Javier La Rosa, led the delegation during the meeting held at the Prime Minister's Office at the Bangladesh Secretariat in the morning, according to a press release issued by the PM's Press Wing.

During the meeting, the delegation discussed increasing Chevron's investment in Bangladesh's existing and mature gas fields, as well as exploring opportunities for investment in new gas fields.

The discussions came amid the government's efforts to strengthen domestic gas production and attract investment to the energy sector to meet the country's growing energy demand.

Title: Court freezes Nagad-linked shares worth Tk786cr
Content:
A Dhaka court has ordered the freezing of shares worth Tk786 crore held by Tanvir Ahmed Mishuk, former managing director of Third Wave Technologies Ltd (later renamed Nagad Ltd), and other individuals and entities linked to an ongoing Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) investigation.

Dhaka Metropolitan Senior Special Judge Md Shahjahan Kabir passed the order today (13 September) following an application by the anti-graft agency.

ACC Assistant Director and investigating officer Mohammad Shahjahan Miraj filed the application seeking the court's order.

According to the application, the ACC is investigating allegations including the siphoning of government funds through unauthorised distributors, the transfer of shares to non-resident investors without bringing foreign currency through legal channels, the use of proceeds from zero-coupon bonds to repay foreign loans, money laundering abroad and the acquisition of assets beyond known sources of income.

The ACC's preliminary investigation found that between 1 April 2021 and December 2024, unused government allowance funds distributed through Nagad were allegedly diverted through software manipulation to 24,159 fake entrepreneur wallets.

The funds were subsequently allegedly routed through bank accounts linked to 648 fake distributor service outlets and 34 unauthorised distributors, according to the application.

The ACC said its preliminary investigation had uncovered evidence of embezzlement amounting to Tk1,706 crore.

According to the application, the allegedly embezzled funds were subsequently layered through various bank accounts and used to purchase shares worth a substantial amount.

Title: Writ filed seeking HC ban on romance-based films, dramas
Content:
A lawyer has filed a petition with the High Court seeking a ban on the production and broadcast of films and dramas based on love and romance, arguing that such content could have a harmful impact on youths and society

Advocate Md Mahmudul Hasan Mamun filed the writ petition today (13 September) at the relevant branch of the High Court.

The cabinet secretary, secretaries of the Information and Broadcasting Ministry and Cultural Affairs Ministry, and chairman of the Bangladesh Film Certification Board have been made respondents.

In the petition, Mamun said excessive romantic content in mainstream films and dramas was contributing to the moral degradation of young people, social disorder and distraction from studies and careers.

He alleged that some films and dramas portray extramarital affairs, adultery and rape as normal or glamorous, creating negative effects on youths and society.

The petition cited reports by international media outlets, including Hindustan Times, Daily Sabah and The New York Times, in support of claims that unrestricted romantic and provocative content can affect young people's psychological development and contribute to violence and crime against women.

Mamun also argued that freedom of speech and expression under Article 39 of the Constitution is subject to reasonable restrictions in the interests of decency and morality.

The writ further seeks mandatory directions for the production and broadcast of films and dramas based on science, education, history, the Liberation War and national defence to encourage creativity and patriotism among young people.

Mamun had earlier sent a legal notice to the respondents on 27 August, seeking action on the issue. He said he filed the writ in the public interest after receiving no response or effective administrative action following the notice.

The lawyer had drawn widespread discussion and criticism on social media after sending the legal notice.

Title: Hartals, strikes against court verdicts, orders are illegal: High Court
Content:
The High Court has declared calling a strike or hartal against a court verdict or order illegal, directing the authorities to take legal and criminal action against organisations that announce such programmes.

A bench of Justice Shashank Shekhar Sarkar and Justice Faysal Hasan Arif delivered the verdict today (13 September), making absolute a rule issued in this regard.

The court observed that court verdicts are binding on all under Article 112 of the Constitution. While parties have the right to appeal against a judgment, calling a strike or hartal in protest against it is illegal and contrary to the Constitution.

The High Court directed the home secretary, Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) and Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) to take legal and criminal action if any strike or hartal is called against a court verdict or order.

Senior Advocate Manzill Murshid appeared for the writ petitioner. Deputy Attorney General Mohammad Ahsan Habib represented the state, while Advocate Asibul Huq appeared for the BRTC and Advocate Md Rafiul Islam for the BRTA.

The rule originated from a writ petition filed by Human Rights and Peace for Bangladesh after transport owners announced a strike following the conviction of a bus driver over a road crash that killed five people, including filmmaker Tareque Masud and journalist Mishuk Munier.

The accident occurred in August 2011 in Manikganj's Ghior upazila when a Delux Paribahan bus collided with a microbus.

The Additional District and Sessions Judge's Court of Manikganj sentenced the bus driver on 22 February 2017, after which transport owners announced a strike.

Following a hearing on the rights organisation's writ petition, the High Court issued a rule on 1 March 2017, asking why calling a strike or hartal against a court verdict should not be declared illegal.

Speaking to reporters today, lawyer Manzill Murshid said the court had made the rule absolute and issued directions to the home secretary, BRTA and BRTC.

He said the court had held that although an appeal against a verdict is available, calling a strike or hartal against a court verdict or order cannot be accepted as it is illegal and contrary to the Constitution.

Title: Man sentenced to death for burning wife to death over dowry
Content:
A Dhaka court today (13 September) has sentenced Dulal Hossain alias Dulu alias Jewel to death for burning his wife to death over a dowry demand in Keraniganj.

Judge Munshi Md Moshiar Rahman of Dhaka Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal-4 handed down the verdict. The convict was also fined Tk2 lakh, Public Prosecutor Md Ershad Alam confirmed.

The tribunal also directed the Dhaka district magistrate or collector to realise the fine by selling the convict's movable and immovable properties and hand over the money to the victim's family.

The tribunal acquitted four other accused because the charges against them could not be proved. The acquitted accused are Dulal's brother Harun, sister-in-law Morshena, sister Sumaiya, and brother-in-law Raju.

According to the case statement, Sharmin married Dulal in 2001, and the couple had a daughter.

Since their marriage, Dulal, acting on the advice and instigation of the other accused, had allegedly demanded Tk2 lakh in dowry from Sharmin's family and physically assaulted her.

At around 9:30am on 17 September 2016, Sharmin was assaulted over the dowry demand before kerosene was poured on her body, and she was set on fire, according to what she later told her mother.

Hearing her screams, local people rescued her. They first took her to Mitford Hospital and later admitted her to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

Sharmin's mother, Mst Momela, went to the hospital after learning about the incident and found her daughter in critical condition. She was informed that 85% of Sharmin's body had been burned.

Sharmin died while undergoing treatment on 30 September that year.

Her mother later filed a case with Keraniganj Model Police Station against six people, including Dulal's mother Jorina.

After completing the investigation, Keraniganj Model Police Station Sub-Inspector AKM Saiduzzaman submitted a charge sheet against all six accused on 31 January 2017.

Title: Ecnec to consider 15 projects at third meeting on Wednesday
Content:
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (Ecnec ) is set to hold its third meeting of the 2026-27 fiscal year on Wednesday (16 September), with a 15-project agenda spanning transport, defence, health, water resources and land management sectors, according to a notice issued by the Planning Division.

The meeting will be held at 10am at the Cabinet Room of Secretariat, chaired by Prime Minister and Ecnec Chairman Tarique Rahman, according to the notice.

Under the Physical Infrastructure Division, the committee will examine Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit Development Project (Line-5): Southern Route, to run from September 2026 to August 2033 under the Road Transport and Highways Division.

Also on the list are upgradation of district highways under Rajshahi Road Zone and under Chattogram Road Zone in its third phase ,both under the same division.

Defence-related infrastructure proposals include the second phase of Barisal Cantonment establishment (July 2026-December 2030) and construction of accommodation and other facilities for naval personnel in the Khulna Naval Zone (July 2026-June 2029), both proposed by the Ministry of Defence.

The Khulna Drainage System Development Project (first revised), running since July 2020 through June 2027 under the Local Government Division, is also listed, alongside two railway projects from the Ministry of Railways: the Implementation of Electric Traction Along the Narayanganj-Dhaka-Joydebpur Section of Bangladesh Railway and the first-revised project for a new dual-gauge railway line from Bogura to Sirajganj.

Under the Industries and Energy Division, Ecnec will review the Improved Working Condition and Social Protection for Workers in the Textile and Leather Sector project from the Ministry of Labour and Employment, and the first-revised upgradation and expansion of the electricity distribution system in Manpura island area under the Power Division.

Three proposals fall under the Socio-Economic Infrastructure Division, all from the Health Services Division of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Financial Institutions Division: Health System Strengthening through MNCH Services Improvement and NCDs Control ,Integrated Health System Response to Fight Against TB, HIV/AIDS and Malaria in Bangladesh ,and Financial Sector Support Project-II or FSSP-II.

Rounding off the approval list under the Agriculture, Water Resources and Rural Institutions Division are the construction of the Musapur Regulator with integrated flood and river management and drainage improvement of the Chhoto Feni and Bamni rivers, part-1 from the Ministry of Water Resources, and the second-revised Digital Land Management System project, covering digital land surveys in three city corporations, one pourashava and two rural upazilas (July 2018-December 2028) from the Ministry of Land.

The notice also lists 15 additional projects already approved by the minister concerned to be placed before Ecnec for information.

These include the second-revised Automation of Land Management project and the first-revised construction of the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society's national headquarters, both from the Ministry of Land and the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief respectively.

Also featured are the first-revised Establishing Green Belt at Bhasan Char and Reforestation of areas affected by Rohingyas in Cox's Bazar, from the Ministry of Environment and a project on strengthening research, conservation and development of indigenous poultry from the Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock.

Infrastructure items on this list include the first-revised establishment of a telecommunication network in economic zones, replacement of ageing and risky bridges in the Rangpur zone, construction of an RDA building from the fifth to tenth floor, construction of a quarter guard and ancillary infrastructure at Jalalabad Cantonment, and preparation of a Digital Elevation (3D) Model of Sylhet division to enhance flood forecasting capacity.

Education, social welfare and sports-related projects for information include infrastructure development at Cantonment Public School and College, Saidpur; further infrastructure development at Military Collegiate School, Khulna; the first-revised Strengthening Social Protection for Improved Resilience, Inclusion and Targeting (SSPIRIT) project; and development works at the Barguna and Dinajpur district stadiums.

Title: 'Clarify which border, which December you will return': Whip Dulu to Hasina
Content:
Whip M Ruhul Quddus Talukder Dulu, chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Science and Technology, has asked Sheikh Hasina to clarify which December she plans to return to Bangladesh.

"Please make it clear which December you will come to Bangladesh. We have seen many Decembers in our lives. Many Ramadan, Eid, Puja festivals and monsoons have also passed. Is it December 2030 or December 2050? Please make it clear," he said.

Dulu made the remarks at a discussion titled "Achievements of the Current Government" at the National Press Club today (13 September), organised by the Uttaranchal Jatiyatabadi Forum.

He also warned that threats and intimidation would not be allowed to disrupt the country's democratic process, saying, "We have come to power with the mandate of the people."

The whip also asked Hasina to clarify which border she would use to enter Bangladesh, saying around 2,000 students and members of the public were killed during the July uprising and that the families of those killed or subjected to enforced disappearance over the past 17 years were waiting for her.

"Justice will be delivered for every killing committed over the past 17 years. This time, you will have to go to Kashimpur Jail. You will have to face justice before the people of Bangladesh," Dulu said.

'PM Tarique Rahman working from 9am to midnight' Speaking about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's work over the past six months, Dulu said the prime minister had been working from 9am until around midnight since taking office after the election to rebuild a "devastated Bangladesh".

"He does not take any protocol. Since independence, he is the only prime minister who has broken all government rules and protocols. He has set an example," Dulu said.

He said Tarique had instructed that there should be no discrimination in road movement for his protocol, recalling incidents in the past when roads were not cleared even when critically ill patients died.

Dulu said the government had waived agricultural loans of up to Tk10,000 for farmers and introduced farmer cards. It had also introduced Family Cards for vulnerable women and started providing honorariums to imams, muazzins and religious leaders of different faiths, he said.

He further claimed that no one had been subjected to enforced disappearance during the past six months and that political opponents had not been intimidated, detained or disappeared.

"The government is trying to resolve people's problems, including those related to gas and electricity. InshaAllah, all problems will be resolved. The government is working to restore a healthy democratic process," Dulu said.

Dulu comments on Awami League procession Referring to a recent Awami League procession, Dulu said, "They held a procession during prayer time. They do not even pray, nor do they believe in Allah."

Mahmuda Habiba, a reserved-seat member of parliament and chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education, said the government had repaid Tk25,000 crore in foreign loans within its first five months in office and was working to reduce the interest burden.

She also said the government was returning surplus funds to the bank accounts of Hajj pilgrims who performed Hajj this year under government management, calling it "unprecedented not only in Bangladesh but anywhere in the world".

Title: Sagar-Runi murder: Family members seek trial at International Crimes Tribunal
Content:
The family of journalist couple Sagar Sarwar and Meherun Runi has filed a written complaint with the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT), seeking a proper investigation and justice for their murders.

Runi's brother, Nawsher Al Roman, submitted the complaint to ICT Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam on behalf of the family today (13 September).

Speaking to journalists after receiving the complaint, Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam said the prosecution team would examine, in accordance with the law, whether the 2012 murder of Sagar and Runi falls within the jurisdiction of the International Crimes Tribunal and whether the case can be tried there.

"If any new information emerges from a preliminary examination, it would be handed over to the relevant task force, he said."

A special task force is investigating the case under a High Court directive, with the investigating officer seeking 129 extensions to submit the report to the lower court.

According to the written complaint, Sagar Sarwar, news editor of Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, a senior correspondent of ATN Bangla, were murdered at their rented residence in West Rajabazar between 2am and 7am on 11 February 2012.

The complaint said that despite investigations by several agencies over the past 14 years, the perpetrators have not been identified and the case remains unresolved.

After the local police, Detective Branch and Rapid Action Battalion failed to resolve the case, the High Court directed that the investigation be handed over to the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI).

However, the investigation has yet to produce a conclusive result, the complaint said. The family has therefore sought a fair and proper investigation through the International Crimes Tribunal to identify the actual perpetrators and bring them to justice.

They also demanded exemplary punishment for those responsible and urged the tribunal to register the complaint and take necessary legal action.

Title: Healthcare system must identify risks and diseases before they become severe: Zubaida
Content:
Renowned cardiologist and Ziaur Rahman Foundation (ZRF) Vice President Dr Zubaida Rahman today (13 September) said the healthcare system must identify health risks and diseases before they become severe, stressing that healthcare is not a privilege but a basic human right.

"Our healthcare system cannot be built around treatment alone. We often say prevention is better than cure, and that remains true. The healthcare system must identify risks and diseases before they become severe," she said.

Zubaida made the remarks while addressing a special international seminar titled "Health Innovation for All: Expanding Access to Affordable and Inclusive Care" as the chief guest on the second day of the three-day "Bangladesh Innovation Fair 2026" at Novo Theatre in the capital's Agargaon.

The session focused on technology-driven ways of delivering modern healthcare at affordable costs to marginalised communities.

Zubaida said the sophistication of hospitals or the advancement of technology could not be used alone to judge the level of healthcare in a country.

She said many people reach specialist hospitals only after their conditions have become complicated, while patients often travel long distances because necessary services are unavailable closer to their homes. "Modern tertiary healthcare has also become extremely expensive. But this is not only for Bangladesh; many advanced countries are facing this worldwide," she said.

The ZRF vice president said the goal should be to make healthcare accessible even in the remotest villages of Bangladesh.

"We want to make healthcare accessible to the remotest villages of our country. More than 90,000 villages in our country should receive accessible healthcare for every citizen of Bangladesh," she said.

Zubaida called for strengthening dengue awareness programmes and encouraging measles vaccination so that no one misses it.

Describing cardiovascular diseases as one of the major causes of disability and death in Bangladesh, she said, "Simple lifestyle preventive measures combined with excellent treatment facilities can change this scenario."

The ZRF vice president also called for extensive cancer awareness programmes.

About diabetes, she said that although Bangladesh has internationally reputed institutions and expertise in healthcare, many people continue to live with diabetes without knowing it.

Zubaida stressed that every screening programme should be connected to confirmatory diagnosis, counselling, treatment, medicines, monitoring and referral.

She said Bangladesh could also begin preparing for the health needs of an ageing society, including dementia, Parkinson's disease and other diseases affecting geriatric populations.

The cardiologist said the country's health vision should be based on a clear principle that quality healthcare should not be a privilege determined by income, location or social status. "It should be accessible to every citizen in every part of Bangladesh," she said.

She said the vision includes strengthening primary healthcare, bringing care closer to home, expanding preventive programmes, developing the health workforce and gradually increasing public investment in health towards 5% of gross domestic product.

"The planned recruitment of 100,000 health workers, particularly, gives an opportunity for women and can create the human foundation for this transformation," Zubaida said.

She said the health workers could support screening, maternal and child health, health education, chronic disease management and referrals within communities.

"In our country, women travel miles in inadequately equipped transport in the late stages of pregnancy or in cases of pre-eclampsia. Prematurely born babies have no proper facilities to thrive," Zubaida said.

She stressed the need for a smooth referral system to move patients from community and primary care facilities to district and specialist hospitals.

The ZRF vice president also called for a nationally coordinated system covering voluntary blood donation, safe collection, infectious disease screening, component separation, storage, transportation and complete traceability from donor to patient. "We need to move towards establishing a national plasma transport technology," she said.

She said innovation will be central to all these efforts, but innovation does not always mean inventing an expensive machine or launching another application. "The most valuable innovation is the one that solves a real problem for patients around the country," she said.

Zubaida said Bangladesh already has many of the institutions needed to make such a transformation possible.

"We have respected researchers, a strong pharmaceutical base, experienced clinicians, expanding digital capability, community-level organisations, and an energetic generation of entrepreneurs," she said, adding that what is often missing is the connection between them.

The ZRF vice president said research could connect with validation, validation with regulation, regulation with responsible procurement, and innovation with service delivery.

She said the next chapter could connect Bangladesh's innovative capacity with an inclusive national healthcare system that finds illness earlier, brings care closer to home, guarantees the foundations of safe treatment and protects families from avoiding financial hardship. "Let us use this innovation fair not only to discuss what is possible, but to agree on what we will begin doing now," she said.

The three-day fair, being held under the theme "Innovate to Market", will end tomorrow (14 September).

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated the event yesterday (12 September), with research teams from various universities and research institutions across the country participating alongside innovators.

Title: Rampal power plant unit shuts down, generation falls by half
Content:
A unit of the Rampal coal-fired power plant in Bagerhat shut down due to a technical fault today (13 September), cutting the plant's power generation by roughly half, even as Adani Power's Godda plant resumed supply from its previously offline unit.

The second unit of the 1,320MW Rampal power plant stopped operating around 11am.

Confirming the matter to The Business Standard, the power plant's General Manage (Human Resources) Anwarul Azim said, "The second unit had been completely shut down due to a technical fault. It will take at least four days to resume operations."

"The work was underway to restore the unit, while the first unit remained operational and continued supplying electricity to the national grid," he added.

The official, however, could not specify the nature of the technical fault.

According to Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) and Power Grid Company of Bangladesh (PGCB) sources, before the shutdown, the plant was generating more than 1,100MW. Its output subsequently fell to below 600MW.

Meanwhile, Adani Power's second unit resumed electricity supply to Bangladesh's national grid at around noon after being shut down due to a technical problem late Thursday night (10 September).

The combined supply from Adani's two units crossed 1,046MW around 2pm, compared with a maximum of around 758MW earlier in the day. The supply could rise further in the afternoon, according to BPDB and PGCB sources.

Adani Power's Godda plant in Jharkhand, India, has an installed capacity of 1,600MW across two 800MW units. The BPDB signed a power purchase agreement with Adani in 2017.

The plant has previously supplied more than 1,500MW to Bangladesh, depending on demand.

The plant had been operating at reduced capacity for about a month due to coal shortages caused by disruptions to coal transportation following a storm.

Its generation increased towards the end of last month, with the plant supplying around 900MW during the day and up to 1,200MW from the evening until midnight.

Its output crossed 1,430MW around 1am on 9 September before one of its units shut down, bringing generation below 750MW.

After the second unit resumed operation today, Adani's supply to the national grid began increasing.

Rampal plant's coal supply improves

According to the plant sources, the 1,320MW Rampal power plant, jointly built by Bangladesh and India, had previously faced production cuts due to coal shortages. Its generation had recently increased to more than 1,100MW after coal supplies improved.

The project was initiated as a joint venture between Bangladesh and India in 2010. On 29 January 2012, the BPDB and India's NTPC Ltd signed an agreement, leading to the formation of Bangladesh-India Friendship Power Company (Pvt) Ltd (BIFPCL).

Under BIFPCL, construction of the 1,320MW Maitree Super Thermal Power Project, commonly known as the Rampal power plant, began after 1,034 acres of land were acquired in Sapmari-Kai-Gordashkathi mouzas under Rajnagar and Gourambha unions of Rampal upazila.

The project was built at a cost of around Tk16,000 crore.

The plant's first unit began generation on 23 December 2022, while the second unit started trial generation on 24 October 2023. Commercial operations officially began on 12 March 2024.

However, the plant's generation has been disrupted more than 30 times since it began commercial operations due to technical faults and other reasons, according to reports.

With the second unit now offline, efforts are underway to restore it, while the first unit continues to supply electricity to the national grid.

Title: Cyber law aims to protect journalists, curb cyberbullying and ensure online decency: Salahuddin
Content:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed today (13 September) said the proposed Cyber Security (Amendment) Act 2026 will help restore decency in the digital space, protect women and young people from cyberbullying and ensure professional safeguards for journalists while preventing any misuse of the law.

"The government is highly conscious of citizens' freedom of expression and personal security," he said.

He made the remarks during a courtesy meeting with a delegation of the International Republican Institute (IRI) at his office at the Bangladesh Secretariat.

The minister said every citizen has the right to express opinions and make constructive criticism subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 39 of the Constitution.

"But constructive criticism is not the same as character assassination or abusive language for political purposes," he said.

Salahuddin said the government has been consulting international and local stakeholders, including media personalities, senior editors and civil society representatives, for the past two months to further refine the proposed cyber law.

He said the government would welcome positive recommendations from both international and local stakeholders to strengthen digital security and ensure a violence-free political environment.

The minister said this as the meeting discussed measures to prevent cybercrime and online bullying and various aspects of the proposed Cyber Security (Amendment) Act 2026.

The IRI delegation, led by its Resident Programme Director John Fluharty, apprised the minister of its ongoing programmes on youth leadership development and promoting violence-free political practices.

Fluharty said young people and political activists in Bangladesh are increasingly facing harassment and reputational attacks through cyberbullying and organised disinformation.

He called for a consensus-based policy and legal protection for both ruling and opposition political groups.

The minister said the government will welcome constructive recommendations from both international and local stakeholders to strengthen digital security and establish a violence-free political environment.

Additional Home Secretary (Political and Immigration Wings) Dr Ziauddin Ahmed and Joint Secretary of the Political-1 Branch Rebeka Khan, among others, attended the meeting.

Title: UCB Investment, Rupali Investment hold capital market stakeholders’ meet
Content:
UCB Investment Limited and Rupali Investment Limited have jointly organised a stakeholders' meeting to discuss the capital market's role in supporting Bangladesh's economic growth and strengthening the banking sector's capital base.

The event, titled "Capital Market Stakeholders Meet – Unlock Possibilities in the Next Chapter of Progress", was held recently at The Westin Dhaka, bringing together investors and other market participants, according to a press release.

Participants discussed regulatory initiatives and reforms being introduced by the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) to support capital market development.

Speakers stressed the importance of private-sector and industrial investment in sustaining economic growth. They highlighted the role of banks, financial institutions and the capital market in channelling funds into productive sectors, alongside the need to strengthen banks' capital positions.

United Commercial Bank PLC (UCB) Chief Executive Officer Mohammad Mamdudur Rashid said the bank had focused on improving its liquidity, loan management, recovery efforts and financial capacity over the past two years.

"As a result, the bank is now firmly moving from stability towards sustainable growth. Our ongoing rights share issue will further strengthen the bank's capital base and enhance its capacity for future growth," he said.

"In this journey, the confidence and participation of our shareholders and capital market stakeholders are extremely important to UCB."

Rupali Investment Limited Chairman and Rupali Bank PLC Managing Director Kazi Md Wahidul Islam described UCB's recent turnaround as a notable example in the banking sector.

"Strong leadership, timely decision-making, and clear strategic direction have played a significant role in driving this progress. Rupali Bank and Rupali Investment will continue to stand alongside UCB as partners in this journey and work together in the broader interest of the country's economy," he said.

Dhaka Stock Exchange PLC Director Minhaz Mannan Emon said, "The banking sector was devastated during the fascist regime. Subsequently, the sector has been striving to recover. In this regard, UCB has set an example. UCB is a reliable institution for share investors, and it has already proven its credibility."

Rupali Investment Limited Chief Executive Officer Md Fokhrul Hasan and UCB Investment Limited Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Tanzim Alamgir also spoke at the event.

Participants discussed the banking sector's capital challenges, citing an aggregate capital shortfall of approximately Tk2.78 lakh crore as of 31 December 2025. They explored ways to address these constraints and restore banks' capacity to support business expansion and economic activity.

The discussion also highlighted UCB's progress over the past two years, with participants sharing recommendations on strengthening its position and supporting future growth.

UCB Investment Limited and Rupali Investment Limited are serving as joint issue managers for UCB's rights share issue.

The organisers said continued engagement among investors, issuers, intermediaries and regulators could strengthen market confidence and support a deeper and more effective capital market.

Title: Standard Chartered holds inaugural Financial Markets Leadership Forum
Content:
Standard Chartered Bangladesh has held its inaugural Financial Markets Leadership Forum for financial institution clients, bringing together regulators and nearly 200 industry leaders to discuss market stability, risk management and opportunities for sustainable growth.

Participants from banks, financial institutions and capital markets shared perspectives on Bangladesh's evolving financial markets and regulatory landscape, according to a press release.

Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Masud Khan attended as the chief guest, while Bangladesh Bank Deputy Governor Md Sarwar Hossain attended as the special guest.

Discussions focused on how stronger risk management, deeper and more liquid markets, technology and sustainable finance could help Bangladesh navigate global uncertainty and pursue new opportunities.

Participants also highlighted the importance of robust market infrastructure, regulatory clarity and collaboration in strengthening Bangladesh's position within the global financial system.

Standard Chartered Bangladesh CEO Enamul Huque delivered the opening remarks.

"Bangladesh's financial markets stand at a pivotal moment," he said. "By deepening market liquidity, strengthening risk management, and embracing digital and sustainable finance, we can unlock the next phase of growth for our economy."

He said the bank would continue working with regulators and clients to help build a more resilient and inclusive financial system, and thanked the guests, speakers, panellists and participants for their contributions.

Standard Chartered Bangladesh Head of Markets and Corporate Sales Sabah Saleheen Azim moderated the event and panel discussion.

Other speakers and panellists included City Bank PLC Managing Director Mashrur Arefin and Eastern Bank PLC Deputy Managing Director and Head of Treasury, Offshore Banking and Financial Institutions Mehdi Zaman.

Standard Chartered participants included Head of Markets FI Sales South Asia Ashish Malik; Head of FI, GCNA, and Head of BBD, GCNA South Asia, CIB FI BBD Himanshu Dhyani; and Head of Financial Institutions, Bangladesh Nasreen Rehman.

The bank said it remained committed to supporting reforms, strengthening collaboration and building confidence across the financial system, drawing on more than 120 years of continuous presence in Bangladesh.

Title: KBCCI holds seminar on national budget 2026–27, business implications
Content:
The Korea-Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce & Industry (KBCCI) has organised a seminar on the national budget for 2026–27, examining fiscal and regulatory changes and their implications for businesses and investors.

The seminar, titled "Navigating the National Budget 2026–2027: Opportunities for Business and Investors", was held at Hotel Sheraton in Banani, Dhaka, according to a press release.

Senior government officials, diplomats, business leaders, representatives of Korean companies, investors and KBCCI members attended the programme.

Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to Bangladesh Kim Ji-joon attended as the chief guest, while National Board of Revenue (NBR) Member Md Moazzem Hossain and Invest Bangladesh Executive Member Nahian Rahman Rochi attended as special guests.

Welcoming participants, KBCCI President Shahab Uddin Khan highlighted how changes in tax, VAT, customs duties and import policies directly affect business costs, investment decisions and future planning.

He reaffirmed the chamber's commitment to strengthening Bangladesh–Korea economic relations through trade and investment, joint ventures, technology transfer and industrial cooperation.

Snehashish Barua, FCA, ACA (ICAEW), delivered the keynote presentation, titled "Finance Act 2026 Unveiled: Analysis of Key Tax, VAT, Customs & Regulatory Changes". He discussed major fiscal and regulatory changes and their practical implications for businesses and investors.

The special guests also shared perspectives from the NBR and Invest Bangladesh.

In his address, Ambassador Kim Ji-joon emphasised translating the momentum of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) into joint-venture manufacturing and foreign investment.

He highlighted the need for a level playing field for formal investors, an investment-friendly tariff structure, integrated industrial clusters and predictable incentives for joint ventures.

Other priorities included easier visa and work-permit procedures for foreign experts, stronger digital connectivity among customs, ports, banks and tax authorities, and effective support for existing investors alongside reliable energy supplies.

The ambassador reaffirmed Korea's readiness to remain a long-term partner of Bangladesh in investment, technology transfer and manufacturing expertise.

The programme concluded with a vote of thanks by KBCCI CEO Do-Kee Park (Harry), followed by a networking session.

KBCCI said it would continue facilitating dialogue between policymakers and the private sector to create business and investment opportunities and strengthen economic ties between Bangladesh and Korea.
Author: Press Release

Content:
Retail technology and distribution platform PriyoShop has launched a scholarship programme to support the education of children of employees working across its hubs.

Under the "PriyoShop Scholarship" initiative, selected students have received a one-time education grant and will receive continued academic support to help them pursue higher education, according to a press release.

The recipients were selected from among hub employees' children who recently achieved outstanding results in their Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examinations. The company said the initiative recognised students who had excelled despite challenges and limited opportunities.

PriyoShop Founder and CEO Asikul Alam Khan, along with other members of the leadership team, presented the scholarships to the recipients in the presence of their parents.

The company said the programme reflected its recognition of the role employees' families play in supporting its operations and growth.

PriyoShop operates 43 hubs across Bangladesh, where employees serve thousands of retailers nationwide.

Speaking on the occasion, Asikul Alam Khan said, "Every achievement of PriyoShop carries the hard work of our colleagues and behind them, the support of their families. That's why we believe our responsibility doesn't end with our employees alone; it extends to their families and to the generations that follow."

He added, "This scholarship is not just financial support, it is a long-term commitment from us. We want these students to keep moving toward their dreams and to know that PriyoShop stands with them."

PriyoShop said the scholarship programme aimed to create educational opportunities for employees' children and support their academic progress.

Title: Obama voices caution on AI, urges Democrats to tackle it, NYT says
Content:
Former US President Barack Obama has warned that artificial intelligence could be "dangerous" if not properly managed, and urged Democrats to frame ​policy and governance agendas to tackle the issue, the New ‌York Times said today (13 September).

The remarks at a recent private fundraising event come as growing numbers of US lawmakers call for tougher rules on AI systems after ​dire warnings from two Anthropic researchers that rapid industry progress ​risks extinction of the human race.

"This is something that is moving ⁠very fast in private hands, and if we don't get on ​top of it, I think can be dangerous," the newspaper quoted Obama ​as saying on Thursday (10 September).

Citing a partial transcript of remarks from Obama's office, the paper said he encouraged House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries to help shape a public ​conversation on AI policy if Democrats regained the House in midterm ​elections on 3 November.

"Once you are speaker, I would strongly urge that the Democrats ‌put ⁠together a framework for a very public conversation," Obama told Jeffries, the paper added.

He also called for candidates in the 2028 presidential race to make AI one of their central agendas, with a very clear ​plan to tackle ​the surrounding ⁠safety and economic concerns, the paper said.

Obama's office did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

The ​extinction concerns were spurred by cases of AI agents ​going rogue ⁠to hack external systems and AI safety researchers quitting their companies concerned about the technology's risks.

Yesterday (12 September), Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged AI companies to ⁠throttle ​back work on model capabilities amid growing ​fears of AI misuse, prompting agreement from both OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk, ​who runs xAI.

Title: Modi warns against weaponisation of technology, critical minerals at BRICS summit
Content:
As BRICS prepared to wrap up its two-day summit in New Delhi, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi today cautioned against the weaponisation of technology and critical minerals, saying this could hinder shared progress.

In a speech on the concluding day of the BRICS summit at Bharat Mandapam, he said increasing geopolitical tensions are adversely impacting ordinary lives globally and urged BRICS to unite to address these challenges and drive inclusive growth, particularly across the global South.

Modi made the remarks in the presence of top BRICS leaders including Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.

Modi said the world is witnessing increasing tensions, and they are having a significant negative impact on the lives of ordinary people.

"Pandemics, climate disasters, and supply chain disruptions have demonstrated that in today's interconnected world, no crisis remains confined to a single region," he added.

Modi's remarks about weaponisation of critical minerals can be viewed as a message to China, which holds a dominant position in global supply chains for critical minerals and rare earths.

Last year, China tightened its export controls on rare earths and other materials critical for advanced tech manufacturing during trade negotiations with the United States.

China controls more than 90 percent of global rare-earth refining, giving it enormous leverage over critical technologies ranging from the permanent magnets used in EVs and AI data centres to components in advanced electronics and semiconductors.

Modi said a consensus has been reached on a BRICS integrated early warning system for the prevention of and response to infectious diseases.

The guidelines for an early warning data integration mechanism have also been formulated, he said.

Title: Hidden crypto farm in Mexican mountains puts spotlight on cartel funding
Content:
Nestled in the lush green mountains of Central Mexico, next to a sparsely travelled gravel road, few people had reason to wander close enough to hear the loud, mechanical whirring of a clandestine cryptocurrency farm.

What led police to the ramshackle building, suspected of mining virtual coins to launder illicit funds, was not only the noise but the vast amount of electricity needed to power and cool hundreds of specialised computing units, at levels far surpassing the needs of the small communities scattered around the Sierra Norte region of Puebla state.

Crypto mining — which uses powerful computers to generate virtual assets such as bitcoin — represents a new frontier in Mexico's fight against organised criminal groups, which have extended their reach beyond drug trafficking and extortion into the murkier realm of financial crime.

In Puebla, authorities discovered 300 graphics processing units (GPUs), 80 medium-voltage terminals and eight satellite antennae — all geared to compete against millions of other machines to solve puzzles and create valuable new crypto coins.

While a relatively modest operation by international commercial standards, it is the fourth such crypto farm uncovered in the area since early last year.

"Drug cartels appear to have reached a new level of sophistication," said David Saucedo, a Mexico-based security analyst, adding that setting up such an operation would have required technical expertise and backing from a well-financed group, such as one of Mexico's most powerful cartels.

Mexico's federal attorney's office declined to comment, citing an active investigation.

Electricity theft fuels operations

Globally, illicit cryptocurrency transactions more than doubled in 2025, with addresses linked to criminal activity receiving an estimated $154 billion, up from $59 billion a year earlier, according to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, which analysed transaction volumes sent to illicit wallet addresses.

Chainalysis attributed much of the increase to a surge in transactions linked to sanctions evasion, including payments involving sanctioned governments.

As more people and institutions worldwide adopt virtual currency, most within the confines of the law, Latin American cartels are among those increasingly using crypto transfers and mining operations to launder money, said Caio Motta, the firm's Latin American specialist.

"These locations will have very cheap electricity, or be in an area under the influence of organised crime so they're able to steal electricity and establish a large infrastructure to mine cryptocurrency," Motta said.

Electricity is the biggest cost for mining crypto, as energy prices have increased and the process of minting a single unit of virtual currency has become more resource-intensive.

The University of Cambridge's Bitcoin Electricity Consumption Index estimates the cost of minting one bitcoin — the most widely used cryptocurrency — at nearly $45,000. This would still bring a substantial profit when sold at current prices of around $78,000.

"If they were stealing the electricity, the main costs of the operation would be, well — nothing," said Samuel Leon, an expert in energy theft at Mexico's Iberoamericana University, referring to the Puebla operation.

Mexican authorities said they are investigating whether the crypto farm was stealing electricity from a nearby hydroelectric dam.

Hidden in remote mountain terrain

The bushy forests and scattered communities of the Sierra Norte, where the Puebla crypto farm was found, made for an ideal hiding spot.

Two people living in neighbouring communities, who requested anonymity for fear of reprisals, told Reuters that the whirring noise could be heard one kilometre (0.6 mile) away. The crypto farm was located approximately twice that distance from the nearest village.

Three other similar crypto farms were found last year in the vicinity of the nearby hydroelectric dam in northern Puebla. Local authorities said they are collaborating with nearby states to investigate the possibility of more hidden operations.

Similar raids have taken place in Brazil, the US and Southeast Asia, including a major bitcoin mining operation in Thailand that spanned five provinces.

According to Motta of Chainalysis, rising global cryptocurrency use will likely push crypto-related crime to new records in the years ahead, as virtual currencies become more accessible even as investigators improve their ability to trace online transactions.

"Law enforcement agencies are becoming far more equipped to fight organised crime using cryptocurrency," he said.

Title: MPO-listed teachers' eligibility for local polls rests with EC: Shahe Alam
Content:
The Election Commission (EC) will decide whether teachers of private educational institutions under the Monthly Pay Order (MPO) facilities will be allowed to contest local government elections, State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development (LGRD) and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam said today (13 September).

Title: Bangladesh must assess risks before joining Mecca Defence Alliance: Experts
Content:
Bangladesh should assess the proposed Mecca Defence Alliance's structure, obligations and impact on strategic autonomy and ties with India, the US and China before joining, experts said. The alliance could offer defence and economic opportunities, but Dhaka must examine its compatibility with foreign policy and international obligations, they said.

The observations were presented at a roundtable titled "Significance of Mecca Defence Alliance & Options for Bangladesh", organised by the Centre for Strategic and Development Studies (CSDS) and chaired by former ambassador Maj Gen (retd) AMSA Ameen.

Professor Shahab Enam Khan of Jahangirnagar University said Bangladesh should consider the Myanmar situation, including Pakistan's potential role in Rohingya repatriation and its growing defence ties with Myanmar.

"Bangladesh needs a regional partner to keep the OIC channel active. Pakistan could be an important partner in this regard," he said.

China's role in the Bangladesh-Myanmar context also requires Dhaka to balance ties with Washington and Beijing, Shahab said. Changing relations among Saudi Arabia, the Gulf countries, Iran and Türkiye could create diplomatic challenges, while ties with Saudi Arabia, other Gulf states and Qatar remain important, particularly because Bangladesh depends heavily on Qatar for natural gas imports.

He also stressed defence modernisation and diversification, saying these had become more important after 2024. Myanmar's move to establish a nuclear power plant was another concern, he added.

Former ambassador Mahbub Uz Zaman said the pact had so far developed as a joint defence arrangement among three countries, with a key provision treating an armed attack on one member as an attack on all three.

"If Bangladesh joins the agreement, it needs to know under what circumstances it could be required to use force and what kind of international obligations this could create," he said.

Mahbub said membership could affect Bangladesh's "strategic autonomy" and balanced ties with India, the US and China. The pact should also be assessed against Article 25 of the Bangladesh Constitution and relevant principles of the UN Charter, he said.

Professor Shahiduzzaman, a retired international relations professor at Dhaka University, said uncertainty remained over the pact's future structure and sustainability.

Bangladesh should wait for a formal proposal, he said, adding that expansion was unlikely to make significant progress in the next few months. Its future would also depend on relations among Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Türkiye and Iran.

Lt Gen (retd) Aminul Karim said the pact should not be compared directly with Nato because its organisational structure remains unclear. However, Türkiye's military technology, Pakistan's military capabilities and Saudi Arabia's financial resources could benefit Bangladesh's defence and economy.

He called for stronger defence capabilities and credible deterrence, particularly a stronger air force and air defence system, while maintaining good relations with India. Greater defence capability would strengthen Bangladesh's position in talks with India based on sovereign equality, he said.

Former Pakistani senator Mushahid Hussain Sayed, joining virtually, called the alliance a "significant and historic initiative" that could offer Muslim countries a new strategic alternative.

Bangladesh should remain focused on South Asia, he said, while stronger Bangladesh-Pakistan ties and cooperation among Bangladesh, Pakistan and China could help create regional balance.
Author: TBS Report

Title: Larry Ellison cancels plan to sell Oracle stock worth up to $7.5 billion
Content:
Oracle said yesterday (12 September) that its co-founder and executive chairman Larry Ellison had cancelled a plan to sell up to 50 million Oracle shares, worth about $7.5 billion at Friday's (11 September) closing price.

Oracle had disclosed in a regulatory filing Friday (11 September) that Ellison had adopted the trading plan on 22 June 2026, and that it was scheduled to expire on 24 October 2026.

"No Oracle stock was sold under that plan, and he has no other plans to sell any of his Oracle stock," Oracle said yesterday (12 September).

Oracle's stock has taken a beating this year amid growing investor concerns over soaring capital expenditure that has pressured its free cash flow.

The shares are down nearly 23% year to date and were more than 18% below their closing level on 18 June, the last trading day before Ellison adopted the plan.

Oracle did not give a reason for the cancellation of Ellison's trading plan.

Ellison, 82, served as Oracle's CEO until 2014 and is the company's largest shareholder, owning over 38% of the company, according to LSEG data.

Earlier in the week, Oracle had reported quarterly results that topped Wall Street estimates and a smaller cash burn than expected, easing some concerns about its debt-fuelled spending spree and leading to a jump in the shares on Friday.

However, its stock later reversed course as analysts said a recovery in cash flow remained some way off.

The firm also announced that restructuring costs, part of a plan that includes job cuts, will rise by about $700 million.

Oracle / Larry Ellison

Title: Jahangirnagar University team wins DIMFF-UNHCR mobile filmmaking workshop
Content:
A team from Jahangirnagar University has won a month-long mobile filmmaking workshop organised by the Dhaka International Mobile Film Festival (DIMFF) in collaboration with UNHCR, with the closing ceremony held at the University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB) Permanent Campus on 11 September.

The workshop focused on filmmaking and refugee experiences under the theme "Forced to Flee", with participants receiving training in colour grading and other filmmaking techniques, according to a press release.

Participants also learned about the experiences of refugees and UNHCR's work in supporting refugee communities before producing short films based on the workshop theme.

Five teams were shortlisted from 20 participating universities, including the University of Dhaka, ULAB, North South University, Jahangirnagar University and Daffodil International University. The jury selected "MANOB" from Jahangirnagar University as the winning team.

The closing ceremony featured remarks from Professor Dr Sumon Rahman, dean of the School of Social Sciences and head of the Department of Media Studies and Journalism at ULAB, and Mir Wadud Islam, instructor and co-adviser of DIMFF 2027.

Representing UNHCR Bangladesh, Kevin Lindblom, associate external relations officer, highlighted the role of storytelling in building awareness and understanding of refugee experiences.

Jury members Md Hafizuddin Munna and Ishtiyak Ahmad Zihad also shared their observations on the participating films and encouraged young filmmakers to use storytelling to highlight issues and experiences around them.

The winning team said the workshop helped its members discover new skills and explore creative ways of telling stories through filmmaking.

Certificates were distributed among participants at the ceremony in recognition of their involvement in the workshop. As the winning prize, UNHCR will provide the MANOB team with a day-long tour of a Rohingya refugee camp.

The ceremony concluded with a vote of thanks from Syeda Sadia Mehjabin, senior lecturer and adviser of DIMFF 2027. Organisers said the workshop reflected DIMFF's aim of empowering young filmmakers to use mobile technology as a tool for storytelling and communication.
Author: Press Release

Title: Adani power supply rises as Godda plant's Unit-2 synchronised with national grid after 3 days
Content:
Unit-2 of the Godda Thermal Power Plant, owned by Adani Power Jharkhand Ltd, in India's Jharkhand, synchronised with Bangladesh's national grid at 12:04pm today (13 September), three days after it went offline following a technical problem in its feed unit.

With the synchronisation, power supply is expected to increase, creating some breathing space to manage severe load shedding sweeping across the country, Md Zahurul Islam, member (production) of the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB), confirmed to The Business Standard.

The unit will take several hours to reach its optimal generation capacity, officials said.

At 9am, power supply from Adani was recorded at 758MW, according to Power Grid Bangladesh.

Adani has been supplying around 750-760MW since Thursday (10 September), when Unit-2 was shut down following a technical problem with its feed unit. The supply rose to 846MW at 1pm, Power Grid Bangladesh said.

Later, Adani, through its PR agency, said power supply had risen to 1,046MW as of 2pm, with Unit-1 supplying 756.66MW and Unit-2 290MW.

In a short message sent to TBS through its PR agency earlier today, Adani Power said Unit-2 was successfully lit up at 5:17am, ahead of schedule, with synchronisation expected by 11:30am.

Before the unit went offline at around 1am on Thursday, Adani was supplying around 1,430MW to Bangladesh.

A feed unit, also known as a boiler feed pump, in the main water supply system of Unit-2 had developed a fault, forcing the generating unit to shut down.

The boiler feed pump is a critical component of a thermal power plant, as it continuously pumps high-pressure water into the steam boiler. Any malfunction can disrupt boiler operations and trigger an automatic shutdown as a safety measure.

The latest technical disruption follows a series of supply interruptions at the Adani plant in recent weeks.

The plant had earlier reduced generation due to severe congestion on the railway network, which disrupted coal transportation to the Godda plant in India.

Adani Power said restrictions on coal transportation and loading had affected coal availability, prompting it to optimise generation and prioritise supply during evening peak hours.

Adani Power's Godda plant has two units, each with an installed capacity of 800MW. Its combined actual generation capacity, however, is around 1,496MW.

Title: TIFF 2026: K-pop superstar Lisa sparks fan frenzy at documentary premiere
Content:
K-pop star Lisa was met by piercing screams from fans as she walked the red carpet at ​the Toronto International Film Festival for the premiere of her ‌new documentary, "Always Lalisa."

Lisa rose to fame as a member of the K-pop girl group Blackpink, and the film follows a year in her life after ​taking a break from the band to embark on ​a solo career.

"I just tried to find new things — like ⁠what can I do more than this?" she told Reuters ​in an interview after the Friday premiere.

The star, whose full name ​is Lalisa Manobal, said she initially thought a year would be long enough, but is still trying to figure out what she loves and her next challenge.

"Always Lalisa" ​captures her triumphs and setbacks between 2024 and 2025, documenting ​the release of her debut solo album "Alter Ego," her acting debut in HBO's ‌hit ⁠series "The White Lotus" and preparations to perform on her own before huge crowds at the Coachella music festival.

The documentary was directed by Sue Kim, an executive producer on Apple TV's 2024 documentary ​series "K-Pop Idols."

"This is ​this incredible opportunity ⁠to get to know someone who we're only ever given a very specific image of because ​of the music system that she comes from. ​We get ⁠to have this unprecedented access, proximity and exposure to her ... It's not the world of K-pop," Kim told Reuters.

After Lisa's return to ⁠the ​group, Blackpink in February made a return ​with the mini-album "DEADLINE," their first release in more than three years.

"Always Lalisa" opens in cinemas on ​12 October.

Title: The Pentagon is using polygraphs to hunt leakers, but the tests are more theatre than fact
Content:
Atlanta, In August 2026, government investigators subjected roughly 50 military officers and civilian employees on the Joint Staff to polygraph tests as part of an inquiry into press leaks about the Iran war and depleted US munitions, according to The New York Times.

The newspaper described the scope of the investigation as unprecedented in the modern military.

This is not the first time the Trump administration has used polygraphs in this way; in 2025, it directed that a wave of tests be administered across the executive branch to expose minor leaks.

As someone who has taken roughly a dozen polygraphs during my 27-year career with the CIA, I am wary of how the process is understood – and of the certainty its use can appear to convey.

Polygraphs carry an ominous, almost mythological reputation among Americans. The more familiar and unofficial term – lie detector tests – likely fuels that perception. Television crime dramas have done their part, too, often portraying the device as an oracle for uncovering the truth when conventional methods fail.

In those portrayals, the polygraph is not merely a tool – it's a window into the soul.

Among those entering government service, especially in national security, the greater anxiety is not the background check but passing the polygraph. My advice is always the same: Don't lie. It's the best – and perhaps only – guidance for a process that most assessments have concluded is a more subjective interpretation than empirical science.

Why the polygraph persists

Polygraphs are "pseudo-scientific" in that they measure physiological responses such as heart rate, blood pressure and perspiration. The assumption is that liars betray themselves through spikes in those signals. But this presumes a kind of psychological transparency that simply doesn't hold up. A person might sweat and tremble simply from fear, anger or frustration – not deceit.

There also are no specific physiological reactions associated with lying. The National Academy of Sciences in 2003, and the American Psychological Association in a 2004 review, concluded that the polygraph rests more on theatre than fact. A 2019 assessment reached the same conclusion.

Accordingly, polygraph results are not generally admissible in US courts. Only a handful of states – such as Georgia, Arizona and California – permit their use even under limited conditions. And they typically require that both parties agree to admission and a judge to approve it. Unconditional admissibility remains the exception, not the rule.

And yet, inside many national security agencies, polygraphs remain central to the clearance process – a fact I observed firsthand during my time overseeing personnel vetting and analytic hiring within the intelligence community.

While not treated as conclusive, polygraph results often serve as a filter. A candidate's visible discomfort – or the examiner's subjective judgment that a response seems evasive – can stall or end the hiring process.

For instance, I know that government agencies have halted clearances after an examiner flagged elevated reactions to questions about past drug use or foreign contacts, even when no disqualifying behaviour was ultimately documented.

In some cases, an examiner's suggestion that a chart shows an anomaly has led otherwise strong applicants to volunteer details they hadn't planned to share – such as minor security infractions, undeclared relationships, or casual drug use from decades earlier – that, while not disqualifying on their own, reshape how their trustworthiness is perceived.

The polygraph's power lies in creating the conditions under which deception is confessed.

A predictable pattern

No administration has been immune to the impulse to investigate leaks. The reflex is bipartisan and familiar: An embarrassing disclosure appears in the press – contradicting official statements or exposing internal dissent – and the White House vows to identify and punish the source. Polygraphs are often part of this ritual.

During his first term, Trump intensified efforts to expose internal dissent and media leaks. Department guidelines were revised to make it easier for agencies to obtain journalists' phone and email records, and polygraphs were reportedly used to pressure officials suspected of talking to the press. That trend has continued – and, since 2025, escalated.

Policies at the Pentagon now restrict unescorted press access, revoke office space for major outlets and favour ideologically aligned networks. The line between legitimate leak prevention and the surveillance or sidelining of critical press coverage has grown increasingly blurred.

At agencies such as the Department of Homeland Security and the FBI, polygraphs reportedly have been used frequently – and more punitively – to identify internal dissenters. Even "cold cases," such as the leak of the Supreme Court's Dobbs opinion ahead of its overturning of Roe v. Wade, were reopened, despite prior investigations yielding no definitive source.

Government reaction varies

Not all leaks are treated the same. Disclosures that align with official narratives or offer strategic advantage may be quietly tolerated, even if unauthorised. Others, especially those that embarrass senior officials or reveal dysfunction, are more likely to prompt formal investigation.

In 2003, for example, the leak of CIA officer Valerie Plame's identity – widely seen as retaliation for her husband's criticism of the Iraq War – triggered a federal investigation.

The disclosure embarrassed senior officials, led to White House aide Scooter Libby's conviction for perjury, later commuted, and drew intense political scrutiny.

Leaks involving classified material draw the sharpest response when they challenge presidential authority or expose internal disputes. That was the case in 2010 with Chelsea Manning, whose disclosure of diplomatic cables and battlefield reports embarrassed senior officials and sparked global backlash. Government reaction often depends less on what was disclosed than on who disclosed it – and to what effect.

A narrow set of disclosures, such as those involving espionage or operational compromise, elicit broad consensus as grounds for prosecution. But most leaks fall outside that category. Most investigations fade quietly. The public rarely learns what became of them. Occasionally, there is a vague resignation, but direct accountability is rare.

What the future holds

The Pentagon polygraph campaign is not likely to eliminate leaks to the press. But it may have a chilling effect that discourages internal candour while diverting investigative energy away from core security priorities.

Even if such campaigns succeed in reducing unauthorised disclosures, they may come at the cost of institutional resilience. Historically, aggressive internal enforcement has been associated with declining morale and reduced information flow – factors that can hinder adaptation to complex threats.

Some researchers have suggested that artificial intelligence may eventually offer reliable tools for detecting deception but caution that the technology is nowhere near operational readiness.

For now, institutions will have to contend with the tools they have – imperfect, imprecise and more performative than predictive.
