Title: HC directs police to verify arrest warrants via central database
Content:
The High Court today (14 September) directed police not to arrest or harass anyone without properly verifying the arrest warrant through the police's Central Data Management System.

The court also directed authorities to verify the identities of plaintiffs and lawyers when filing cases.

The High Court bench of Justice KM Hafizul Alam and Justice Murad-e-Mawla Sohel issued the directives while disposing of a rule issued in response to a writ petition.

Senior Advocate Manzil Morshed appeared for the writ petitioner, while Deputy Attorney General JR Khan Robin represented the state.

The Human Rights and Peace for Bangladesh (HRPB) filed the writ petition in 2013 after reports were published in various media outlets about people being arrested and harassed through fake arrest warrants.

Following a hearing on the petition, another High Court bench issued the ruling on 30 January 2013.

After the verdict, lawyer Manzil Morshed told journalists that the court directed police officers to verify the authenticity of any arrest warrant through the Central Data Management System before taking steps to arrest anyone.

The court also directed the Inspector General of Police to issue a circular mentioning the court's directives and send it to all law enforcement agencies.

In another order, the court directed the Registrar General of the Supreme Court to send instructions to all lower court judges, including district judges, metropolitan judges, chief judicial magistrates and chief metropolitan magistrates.

The instructions require the identity of plaintiffs and lawyers to be verified when filing any complaint case. A copy of the plaintiff's National Identity Card and the lawyer's professional card must be attached to the case documents for this purpose.

The court said any arrest must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Otherwise, it would constitute a violation of the law.

It also said arrests through fake warrants violate a citizen's fundamental and constitutional rights, and ensuring these rights is the responsibility of all law enforcement agencies.

The court further observed that caution is essential when filing cases and making arrests to prevent people from being harassed through the courts. Otherwise, the damage caused to citizens cannot be compensated.

Title: ShareTrip becomes title sponsor of Monitor Airline of the Year 2026
Content:
Online travel agency ShareTrip has joined the 12th edition of Monitor Airline of the Year as title sponsor, partnering with The Bangladesh Monitor for its annual airline awards.

The Bangladesh Monitor Editor Kazi Wahidul Alam and ShareTrip Limited Co-founder and CEO Sadia Haque signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) at Crowne Plaza Dhaka Airport on 10 September, according to a press release.

Under the agreement, ShareTrip will support the promotion of the awards programme and the organisation of its gala ceremony.

The ShareTrip-Monitor Airline of the Year 2026 awards will recognise airlines operating in Bangladesh for excellence in passenger service across 27 categories.

Winners will be determined primarily through an opinion poll among frequent air travellers. Online voting took place from 21 July to 25 August 2026.

Individuals who had undertaken at least four air trips during 2025 were eligible to participate and vote based on their personal travel experiences.

A jury comprising representatives from different social and professional groups will select the winners based on the poll results.

The winners will be announced at a gala ceremony scheduled for November at Crowne Plaza Dhaka Airport.

Airline of the Year is The Bangladesh Monitor's flagship event, introduced in 2007 and held regularly since then to recognise service excellence among airlines. The organiser describes it as Bangladesh's only airline recognition programme.
Author: Press Release

Title: International Day of Democracy tomorrow
Content:
The International Day of Democracy 2026 will be observed tomorrow (15 September) in countries like elsewhere around the world.

The government and social and political organisations will take different programmes to observe the day.

Marking the International Day of Democracy 2026, United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres emphasised "the importance of bringing together people from across societies to enrich decision making, foster trust and build more peaceful, inclusive and resilient societies."

The United Nations Democracy Fund, United Nations Office for Partnerships will host an event on the International Day of Democracy on Tuesday at UN Headquarters to highlight how deliberative democracy can foster greater agency and ownership by bringing diverse voices into decision-making.

The event will reflect on experiences from citizens' assemblies across the globe and explore how participation, dialogue and inclusion can strengthen trust and contribute to more responsive, accountable and effective governance.

Governance systems can create meaningful opportunities for people to influence the decisions that affect their lives. Through dialogue, collaboration and working to understand different points of view, it can be ensured that no one is left behind.

Title: Trump tells Ukraine's Zelenskiy to stop hitting Russian diesel
Content:
US President Donald Trump on Sunday called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy to stop targeting Russian diesel infrastructure, saying the attacks were causing a shortage of the fuel that is "hurting the world".

A wave of long-distance Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries in recent months has reduced that country's fuel production, triggering gasoline shortages across the country.

Ukraine, which faces regular Russian attacks on its own energy infrastructure, says refineries are legitimate military targets.

The US national average price for diesel, which is used by trucks, trains, ships and farm equipment, rose over $6 a gallon for the first time on Thursday, according to price tracker GasBuddy.

"Mr. Zelenskiy has to do one thing: He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia," Trump told journalists during a visit to the Irish Open, which is being held in the west of Ireland on a golf course owned by his family.

"We spoke to Mr. Zelenskiy about it. There are plenty of other targets. Don't hit diesel fuel. That's hurting the world," he said.

The global shortage "isn't done by the Middle East, this is done by what's happening with Russia and Ukraine," Trump added.

Russia downgraded its oil output forecast for this year to a 17-year low and revised its fuel exports outlook for 2026 and 2027 due to the war, according to a government draft forecast seen by Reuters.

Title: Health minister monitors attendance digitally, orders show-cause notices for absent healthcare workers
Content:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hossain monitored the attendance of doctors, nurses, and healthcare workers through the digital attendance system and ordered show-cause notices against those found absent from work without permission.

The minister carried out the monitoring today (14 September) from his office at the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in Dhaka.

He checked the digital attendance records of Bhurungamari Upazila Health Complex in Kurigram, Belabo and Raipura Upazila Health Complexes in Narsingdi, Aditmari Upazila Health Complex in Lalmonirhat, Lama Upazila Health Complex in Bandarban and Dirai Upazila Health Complex in Sunamganj.

During the monitoring, several doctors, nurses and healthcare workers were found absent from some health facilities. The minister spoke to the concerned civil surgeons and upazila health and family planning officers and directed them to issue show-cause notices to those absent without permission.

"Ensuring the presence of doctors, nurses and healthcare workers at their workplaces is extremely important to ensure healthcare services. Attendance monitoring will be strengthened to ensure that people receive the necessary services at health facilities in their respective areas," the minister said.

He added that he would regularly monitor the attendance of doctors, nurses and healthcare workers at various health facilities across the country from his office.

Health Services Division Secretary Dr ANM Bazlur Rashid and Health Education and Family Welfare Division Secretary AKM Benjamin Riazi were present during the monitoring.

Title: AI-linked stocks slump after top lab CEOs call for slowing technology's development
Content:
AI-connected stocks fell sharply on Monday after the CEOs of the US companies developing the most advanced AI models warned the pace of development must slow to prevent threats to humanity.

Nasdaq e-mini futures fell 1.3% during Asian trade. Shares in ChatGPT-maker OpenAI's investor SoftBank tumbled as much as 13.2% in Japan.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, in a lengthy essay shared on X on Saturday, called on AI companies to slow the rate at which they advance model capabilities amid mounting fears of misuse of artificial intelligence. Both Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, said that they agree with Amodei.

The Anthropic CEO wrote that in six to 12 months, AI agents "could be capable of taking over the entire internet potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage."

OpenAI's Altman also said the company would not proceed with an IPO this year, citing safety concerns.

In Japan, memory chipmaker Kioxia plunged 9.8% initially, while chip supply chain company Tokyo Electron ell 3.7%.

In Taipei, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company slipped 1.2%, while in South Korea SK Hynix slid 5.3% and Samsung Electronics fell 3.7%.

"Selling pressure is likely to hit AI and semiconductor-related stocks in Tokyo following a series of weekend comments calling for a slowdown in the pace of AI development," Takayuki Miyajima, senior economist at Sony Financial Group, said in a note.

"Additionally, uncertainty surrounding the situation in the Middle East continues to weigh on sentiment."

In Shanghai, memory chipmaker CXMT dropped as much as 3.6%, while Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation fell 2.6%.

In Hong Kong, Zhongji Innolight shed as much as 6.7% at one point, while Minimax dropped as much as 7.8%. Shares of Z.ai, the developer of the GLM AI series, also tumbled as much as 10.5% after making a discounted share placement.

"Unacceptable" risks

San Francisco-based Anthropic released a threat intelligence report on Thursday detailing how several actors had used its Claude AI models for activities ranging from weapons development and cyber operations to surveillance and fraud.

Alarm about the potential harm from AI grew when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, stating that the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade."

OpenAI's Altman said in an interview that risks of human extinction posed by AI were "unacceptable".

And while several US lawmakers have raised concern about AI's rapid progress and called for new rules, US President Donald Trump on Sunday likened AI critics to "very negative forces" bringing up scenarios that will not happen, and said he wanted to make sure that the US remains the industry leader.

AI-related trades have powered much of the gains in global equities since OpenAI released ChatGPT in 2022, but more recently cyberattacks by rogue AI agents and public discontent with data centre construction have raised opposition to the development of the industry.

The US and Chinese governments are expected to hold AI safety talks as part of bilateral discussions taking place this month, according to two people briefed on the plans.

But China's state-backed Global Times blasted the Anthropic essay in an editorial, calling it a "Cold War playbook" intended to curb the country's technological development.

Some investors dismissed the warnings from Anthropic and OpenAI.

Michael Burry, whose prescient bets against the US housing market before the 2008 financial crisis were chronicled in the movie "The Big Short", said in a message on X the warnings were "hype and puffery" and "cover for real uncontrollable slowing growth".

Others said the warnings would be an overhang.

"In the short term, these warnings could still weigh on AI and chip stocks," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank in Singapore.

"Their valuations assume both strong demand and a relentless pace of technological progress," she said. "When expectations are this high, even a possible delay can trigger profit-taking."

But the bigger question for markets around AI was who would ultimately earn the return on all the capital being spent on building new capacity, said Sebastien Mallet, portfolio manager at T. Rowe Price in London.

"There is little doubt that AI will change the world," he said. "But that does not necessarily mean every investment being made today will generate an attractive return."

Title: Oman postpones meeting on new shipping route in Hormuz

Title: Celine Dion completes her first full concert in 6 years after overcoming rare illness
Content:
She hit the high F, held it, then blew out a breath and turned to look back at the band — a quick, disbelieving glance toward her musical director. Some 30,000 people read it before they had finished screaming: Celine Dion did it.

It was "All By Myself," the song the Quebec superstar's voice has been measured against since 1996, saved for the encore of her first full concert in more than six years — her first since stiff person syndrome, a rare, progressive neurological disease that attacks the muscles, including those of the throat

Few doubted she could still sing. What nobody knew was whether she could get through a whole show, and then get up and do it again two nights later.

Dion gave the crowd three words: "Je vais bien."

"When she hit that note, I grabbed my friend's arm. I'd been holding my breath without realizing. Then I started crying. 'She's back. She's really back,'" said Élodie Marchand, 42, a primary school teacher from Nantes.

Dion, 58, had not played a full concert since 8 March 2020. She was diagnosed in 2022 with stiff person syndrome, a rare, progressive neurological disease that seized the throat she had been singing with since she was 5. She canceled a world tour, then what was left of it, and went quiet. On Saturday night, 25 songs in 2 hours and 15 minutes at the Plenitude Arena in Nanterre, west of Paris, was the first night of the engagement meant to prove she can work again.

The sold-out run is punishing: 16 shows in five weeks, 10 more booked for May 2027, 26 nights in all before tens of thousands of people each time.

The last time France saw her sing, it lasted four minutes. At the Olympic opening ceremony in July 2024, Dion sang from the Eiffel Tower — one song, one night — and the world called it a resurrection. Saturday she had to do it 25 times, then get up and do it again Wednesday. Stiff person syndrome affects one or two people in a million. It stiffens muscles and sets off spasms violent enough to break bones, triggered by loud noise, by touch, by emotional stress. An arena holding 30,000 people is all three at once. Singing with it, Dion told NBC in 2024, felt like being strangled.

"Touring can be very difficult even when you're 100%," she said in a statement in 2023, canceling the last of her dates.

She cried before she finished the first song. In a Dior gown and a Boucheron necklace, she pressed her hands together in prayer, then missed her cue in "On ne change pas," on the line about the skinny little girl from Charlemagne, Quebec.

"I promised myself I wouldn't cry," she said. The crowd answered by chanting the riff from "Seven Nation Army."

She said she had learned to live with the fragility and made it her reason to keep going. Then she sang for another two hours.

The voice has lost some of its top; it is not the instrument that sold 250 million albums. Every big note is now a decision she makes in front of 30,000 people.

She took most of them. She sang "My Heart Will Go On" and "The Power of Love," then Catalani's "Ebben? Ne andrò lontana" — Maria Callas' signature aria — in pink feathers while fake snow fell. Her disease attacks the larynx. She went for it anyway.

Willo Perron's set put her among gray megaliths, a pop Stonehenge. An 18-voice gospel choir came on in robes.

Michelle Obama watched from the seats. Outside, fans wore sashes reading "Celine Dion 2026," like beauty pageant winners, and T-shirts from the LVMH house that shares her first name.

"My daughter kept saying, 'Mum, we can't go all the way to Paris for Celine,'" said Isabelle Gagnon, 52, a teacher from Montreal. "Tonight my daughter was singing beside me, and I thought: you see? This is why we came."

"In Montreal, you grow up knowing those songs whether you mean to or not," said Antoine Beaulieu, 31, a graphic designer. "I used to pretend I was too cool for Celine. Tonight I knew every word, so clearly that was a lie."

Camille Morel, 38, a pharmacist from Lyon, put her phone away. "I wanted to actually be there," she said. "My voice is completely gone. I'm supposed to be working tomorrow — good luck to them."

Then the encore, and the note: the last "anymore" a cappella, the note bent upward, the orchestra surging in beneath her. She fanned herself, laughing at her own relief.

She closed with two Jean-Jacques Goldman standards and a last line to the room: I love you, my loves. Take care of yourselves.

It had taken her 2,379 days to get back. She has 25 more nights to go.

Title: Turkey detains dozens after sweeping raids targeting LGBTQ+ groups
Content:
Turkish authorities have detained at least 47 people following a series of raids on the offices of LGBTQ+ associations in a probe into prostitution and obscenity, prosecutors said.

The crackdown is part of a campaign that the government says is aimed at protecting family values.

The Istanbul chief prosecutor's office said operations were carried out over the weekend across 12 provinces against 38 suspects, and 26 of them were detained, with authorities seizing drugs, digital equipment, smuggled alcohol and a firearm.

In a separate statement, the Ankara chief prosecutor's office said a further 21 people had been detained as part of an investigation into the LGBTQ+ association Kaos GL and five people were still being sought.

Kaos GL said at least 50 activists had been detained, including more than 10 who were taken in police raids on their homes.

In addition, it said authorities blocked access to dozens of websites and social media accounts linked to LGBTQ+ organisations, activists and rights advocates.

Dubbed "My Family is Safe", the government's crackdown comes as President Tayyip Erdogan promotes a "Decade of Family and Population", an initiative designed to tackle falling birth rates and an ageing demographic.

Rights groups have accused the Turkish government of increasingly targeting the LGBTQ+ community in recent years through a hardening of rhetoric and restrictions.

"The real name of this operation is not 'My Family is Safe'; it is state-led discrimination, politics of fear and the dismantling of civil society," the Turkish Human Rights Association said on X.

Nacho Sanchez Amor, the European Parliament's Turkey rapporteur, said the sweeping wave of arrests was "a shocking escalation" of repression.

"This imposition of a moral agenda is a blatant violation of fundamental rights and Turkey's international commitments taking the country down a dark path," Amor said in a post on X.

Prosecutors said there was evidence that children and underage youths were being inappropriately influenced on issues relating to sexual orientation and gender identity.

Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said investigations coordinated by prosecutors in Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, Aydin and Mersin involved judicial proceedings against 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses across 15 provinces.

Title: Nawazuddin Siddiqui says he got 200 scripts and blank cheques after Gangs of Wasseypur 2 but he rejected all
Content:
Anurag Kashyap's Gangs of Wasseypur 2 catapulted Nawazuddin Siddiqui to fame. The actor recently revealed that he began feeling like a star after the film's critical success.

In a recent interview with NDTV, Nawazuddin recalled receiving as many as 200 scripts after Gangs of Wasseypur 2 was released. However, instead of rushing into his next project, the actor chose not to sign any of them, waiting for the right role. Over the years, Nawazuddin has carved a niche for himself in the entertainment industry, earning critical acclaim for his performances across several films.

Nawazuddin Siddiqui talks about life after Gangs of Wasseypur 2

Talking about life after Gangs of Wasseypur 2, he admitted that he felt like a star after the film and said, "After the release of Gangs of Wasseypur 2, I received at least 200 scripts. Blank cheques were lying on my table. People would say, 'Here's the script, and here's a blank cheque. Write whatever amount you want and give us whatever dates are available.'"

He added, "I didn't pick up a single one of those scripts because I didn't like any of them. I decided I would wait for the right one. I was already used to waiting for work for years, so I thought I could wait another two or three years rather than sign something in haste." However, the actor revealed that he did not have to wait too long and soon started getting work.

Nawazuddin Siddiqui played Faizal Khan in Anurag Kashyap's Gangs of Wasseypur 2. The character, initially portrayed as a laid-back and seemingly aimless man, gradually transforms into a ruthless gangster after enduring personal losses and betrayal. His intense performance became one of the highlights of the film. Released in 2012, Gangs of Wasseypur 2 continued the story of the Khan and Qureshi families' decades-long rivalry and was widely praised for its writing, performances and gritty portrayal of crime in Dhanbad.

About Nawazuddin Siddiqui's recent and upcoming movies

Nawazuddin was last seen in the film Main Actor Nahin Hoon, which was released in cinemas on 8 May. While his performance was highly appreciated, the film received mixed-to-negative reviews from critics. He will next be seen in Tumbbad 2, which also stars Alia Bhatt in a key role.

Hindustan Times reported in March 2026 that Tumbbad 2 is being mounted on a much larger scale than the 2018 original. A massive 7–8-acre set is being built in Mumbai, with an entire city being created for the film's first schedule. The sequel is reportedly being made on a budget of around ₹100 crore, making it one of the biggest horror films to come out of Bollywood.

Production began on 7 April 2026, under the direction of Adesh Prasad. The film is scheduled to hit theatres on 3 December 2027, carrying the tagline, "Pralay Aayega."

Title: Emmy Awards 2026: The shows, stars and stories to watch
Content:
The biggest names in television will gather in Los Angeles for this year's Emmy Awards, with shows such as "Beef", Hacks, Pluribus and The Pitt among the major nominees.

Other series competing for awards include Widow's Bay, DTF St Louis, Slow Horses, The Bear and Abbott Elementary.

The Emmys are among the most important awards in the American television industry. This year's main ceremony will take place today (14 September), at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. It will be hosted by Mariska Hargitay and broadcast live on NBC and Peacock in the US.

Several popular shows, however, have either missed out on nominations or received fewer nominations than expected. Viral hit Heated Rivalry is not eligible for the US Emmys, while the final seasons of Stranger Things and Euphoria have had a smaller presence in the major categories.

The dramas and comedies expected to make an impact

The Emmy nominations are broadly divided into drama, comedy and limited or anthology series.

The Outstanding Drama Series award is considered one of the biggest prizes of the night. Last year's winner, The Pitt, returns with its second season and has received eight acting nominations. Its star Noah Wyle is among those nominated.

Other drama contenders include Pluribus, Slow Horses, The Diplomat and A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, the Game of Thrones prequel.

In comedy, Hacks is one of the strongest contenders. The Hollywood satire has reached its fifth and final season and could add more awards to its already impressive Emmy record.

Its stars Jean Smart and Hannah Einbinder are also competing for acting awards.

Smart has already won four Emmys for Hacks. She has won every time she has been nominated for her performance in the show's previous four seasons. Another victory would take her career total to eight Emmys, putting her level with Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Cloris Leachman.

Other comedy shows competing for major awards include Widow's Bay, Shrinking, Abbott Elementary and Nobody Wants This.

Strong competition in the limited-series race

Netflix's second season of "Beef" is expected to be a major contender in the limited or anthology series categories. Its stars Carey Mulligan and Oscar Isaac are also in the running for acting awards.

However, "Beef" faces strong competition from All Her Fault, The Beast in Me and DTF St Louis.

DTF St Louis already had a successful Creative Arts Emmys weekend. David Harbour and Linda Cardellini won acting awards for the series, while the show also collected awards in other technical categories.

There is also a strong British presence among this year's nominees. Alongside Mulligan are Riz Ahmed for Bait, Rufus Sewell for The Diplomat, Kate O'Flynn for Widow's Bay, and Gary Oldman and Jack Lowden for Slow Horses.

Welsh actor Matthew Rhys is another name to watch. He has been nominated in two different lead acting categories — for comedy series Widow's Bay and limited series The Beast in Me.

Why isn't Heated Rivalry in the nominations?

One of the biggest television hits of the past year, Heated Rivalry, is missing from the Emmy nominations.

The ice hockey romance, starring Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams, did not qualify for the US Emmys because it is a fully financed Canadian production and did not have the required US involvement.

That has surprised some viewers, particularly because the Canadian series Schitt's Creek dominated the Emmys in 2021.

The difference is that Schitt's Creek had US financial and broadcasting connections. These included partnerships involving creator and star Dan Levy and his US-based production company.

Heated Rivalry can instead compete at the International Emmys, which are scheduled to take place in New York in November.

Stranger Things and Euphoria have a smaller role

Two other shows that became especially popular with younger audiences have also had a quieter Emmy campaign than some viewers expected.

The final season of Stranger Things has not appeared in the main categories. It received seven nominations, all in technical areas.

Euphoria, despite having a high-profile cast, received only one acting nomination for Zendaya, who has previously won an Emmy for her performance in the series.

A different format for this year's ceremony

The Television Academy has made several changes to the Emmy ceremony this year in an effort to make the main broadcast more entertaining and leave more time for performances and other features.

Two previous categories — Outstanding Talk Series and Outstanding Scripted Variety Series — have been combined into one Outstanding Variety Series category.

This means talk-show hosts such as Jimmy Kimmel will compete alongside programmes including Saturday Night Live and Last Week Tonight With John Oliver.

Several other awards have also been moved to the Creative Arts Emmy ceremonies. These include supporting acting awards for limited series or movies, as well as directing and writing awards in that category.

The Academy has reduced the number of awards presented during the main telecast from 26 to 19. The aim is to create more space for musical performances, comedy sketches and memorable acceptance speeches.

The 2026 Emmy celebrations are being spread across three dates: the Creative Arts ceremonies took place on 5 and 6 September, followed by the main Primetime Emmy ceremony on 14 September.

When and where can you watch?

The main Emmy ceremony begins at 5pm Pacific Time / 8pm Eastern Time on Monday, 14 September.

It will take place at the Peacock Theater at L.A. LIVE in Los Angeles.

Viewers in the US can watch the ceremony live on NBC or stream it on Peacock.

For viewers in the UK, the ceremony begins at 1am BST on Tuesday morning. There is no scheduled British broadcaster showing the ceremony live, although the BBC News website is providing overnight coverage of the red carpet and ceremony.

Some winners have already been announced

A number of awards were handed out during the Creative Arts Emmys before the main ceremony.

Among the winners were Linda Cardellini and David Harbour from DTF St Louis, who won the supporting acting awards in the limited or anthology series category.

Other guest acting winners included Betty Gilpin for Widow's Bay, Ernest Harden Jr for The Pitt, Shailene Woodley for Paradise and the late Rob Reiner for The Bear.

British actress Julie Andrews won for voice-over performance for Bridgerton. Alan Cumming also won an award for hosting the US version of The Traitors.

Other Creative Arts winners included:

Remarkably Bright Creatures — best movie

South Park — best animated series

Mr. Scorsese — best documentary or nonfiction series

Love on the Spectrum — best unstructured reality programme

Super Bowl Halftime Show Starring Bad Bunny — best variety special

The Creative Arts ceremonies also produced several multiple winners. Widow's Bay led the second night with eight awards, while DTF St Louis won six. The Pitt and Pluribus each collected four.

Mariska Hargitay takes the host's seat

This year's main ceremony will be hosted by Mariska Hargitay, best known for playing Detective Olivia Benson on Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.

Hargitay's long-running crime drama began in 1999 and has remained popular, particularly after gaining new audiences through streaming services.

She has received eight Emmy nominations for her role as Benson and won the award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series in 2006.

Law & Order: SVU is also one of the longest-running live-action primetime dramas in television history. The show is expected to reach its 600th episode when its 28th season airs this autumn. The Television Academy describes it as the longest-running primetime live-action drama in television history.

Hargitay has already won two Emmys this year for her documentary My Mom Jayne, about her mother, actress Jayne Mansfield, who died in a car accident when Hargitay was three years old. The awards came in documentary directing and documentary/nonfiction special categories.

Speaking about her role as host, Hargitay said that telling important stories has been central to her career and described it as an honour to celebrate the people who create television.

With major returning shows, new contenders, several British nominees and a number of changes to the format, the 78th Emmy Awards are set to celebrate another year of television.

Title: IPO for humanoid robot maker Boston Dynamics unlikely in 2027: Executive
Content:
Boston Dynamics, Hyundai Motor Group's humanoid robot unit, is unlikely to pursue an initial public offering next year, a senior executive at the parent company with direct knowledge of the matter said, as it has yet to deploy its flagship Atlas robots at scale and remains unprofitable.

The executive's comments suggest a stock market debut for the US-based robotics company may still be years away, despite investor enthusiasm for Hyundai's robotics ambitions, which helped send automaker Hyundai Motor shares to record highs earlier this year.

"It won't be easy," the executive said when asked whether an IPO was possible next year.

"We need to see conditions and situations," he added, without elaborating. He asked not to be named publicly because the matter is confidential.

Hyundai Motor Group has not publicly disclosed a timetable or valuation target for a potential Boston Dynamics listing. The group did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Boston Dynamics was not available for comment outside business hours.

Since the unveiling of the updated Atlas robot in January at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, investors and analysts have closely watched whether the company would pursue a US IPO for Boston Dynamics to help finance its growth. Analysts have published estimates for the company's sales growth and potential valuations due to increasing interest among investors in the robot maker.

Hyundai bought a controlling stake in Boston Dynamics in 2021, and in July, it announced plans to make the company a wholly owned subsidiary by acquiring SoftBank's roughly 10% stake at an undisclosed valuation.

At the time, media reports said the transaction was likely worth about 500 billion won ($371.51 million).

The South Korean group's push into robotics has drawn attention from investors. Hyundai Motor shares more than doubled earlier this year after it unveiled the production version of its Atlas robot in January, though they have since given up much of those gains amid a lack of updates on its robotics strategy.

Shares of Hyundai Motor, the world's third-largest auto group along with affiliate Kia , are up 25% so far this year, lagging behind a 60% surge in the broader market.

IPO likely years away

Analysts say Boston Dynamics is unlikely to go public in the next few years because humanoid robots are still not able to be deployed widely in factories.

Hyundai has said it is seeking to build a factory capable of producing 30,000 robots a year by 2028 and plans to begin deploying humanoid robots at its US plant in Georgia that year before spreading them across its manufacturing network. Some analysts have said those targets are ambitious.

"I think it might take far more time for humanoid robots to replace human workers at the assembly line," said Kim Hyun-su, a senior fund manager at Seoul-based IBK Asset Management.

"It's not difficult to make robots dancing, but it's challenging to make them carry heavy loads and get involved in manufacturing at plants."

Tesla CEO Elon Musk, whose company is developing the Optimus humanoid robot, has described humanoid robots as "the hardest product to scale manufacturing" that the electric car maker has made.

Boston Dynamics' valuations vary widely. Samsung Securities said market estimates place its value at between 50 trillion won and 100 trillion won.

Kim Joon-sung, an analyst at Meritz Securities, said a Boston Dynamics IPO was more likely to come in 2029 or 2030 because Hyundai first needed to gather large amounts of operational data and improve robots' capabilities before selling them broadly to external customers.

In August, IBK Securities said Boston Dynamics could be valued at 141 trillion won by 2030, when it expects the company to generate about 11 trillion won in revenue.

Boston Dynamics recorded a 2025 loss of 528.4 billion won, according to a filing from Hyundai Glovis, which holds a stake of about 11% in the company. Total losses from 2021 through 2025 totalled nearly 1.7 trillion won, the filing said.

Other Boston Dynamics shareholders include Hyundai Motor, Kia, auto parts maker Hyundai Mobis and Hyundai Motor Group Executive Chair Euisun Chung.

Title: Ferry and passenger boat accidents in Southeast Asia
Content:
Two deadly ferry incidents over the past week in Indonesia and the Philippines have focused attention on maritime safety in Southeast Asia.

Indonesia has more than 17,000 islands and the Philippines has more than 7,600, making ferries an important part of the region's transport networks.

Here are details of some recent maritime accidents involving passenger ferries and tourist boats in Southeast Asia.

Indonesia, September 2026 – Six people died and 129 people were still missing after a passenger ship with 243 people aboard capsized in the Java Sea, which covers the waters between Indonesia's four most-populated islands of Java, Sumatra, Sulawesi and Borneo.

The Java Sea has been the site of a number of major air and maritime accidents, including the sinking of the Tampomas II in 1981, when around 600 people died according to some estimates, and a plane crash in 2007 that killed more than 100 people.

Philippines, September 2026 – At least 76 people died when a ferry carrying more than 130 people caught fire on its way from Manila to Coron in Palawan.

Indonesia, August 2026 – One person died and more than 200 people were rescued after a ferry travelling from the tourist island of Bali caught fire on 12 August in waters off the island of Lombok.

Indonesia, August 2026 – Five people died and 233 passengers and crew were rescued from a ferry that caught fire off Madura island.

Vietnam, July 2026 – At least 15 Indian tourists died when a boat capsized off Vietnam's southern island of Phu Quoc.

Philippines, January 2026 – At least 18 people died when a vessel carrying more than 300 people capsized en route to the southern province of Sulu.

Indonesia, December 2025 – Spanish football coach Fernando Martin and three of his children died after their boat capsized in the Padar Island Strait, near a popular tourist spot.

Title: FastCom AI brings task-based customer service to Bangladesh
Content:
AI agents are moving customer service beyond answering questions to carrying out tasks. In Bangladesh, Dhaka-based Ascend AI is developing its FastCom AI platform to connect customer conversations with businesses' internal systems.

The platform is designed to help companies handle enquiries, retrieve information and complete tasks such as processing orders or registering service requests, while referring cases requiring human judgement to staff.

For years, businesses have used chatbots to handle common customer questions. For many customers, however, the experience has remained frustrating.

Earlier rule-based chatbots typically relied on a fixed set of questions and answers. They often struggled when a conversation required information from internal systems or an action beyond responding.

A newer category of technology, commonly described as agentic AI, is designed to take this further. An AI agent can identify what a customer wants, determine the next step, and carry out a task within limits set by the business.

The distinction is clear in a routine order enquiry. A chatbot without access to a company's order system may be unable to provide an update, while an AI agent connected to that system can look up the order and return its status.

Depending on its configuration, the agent could also register a complaint, initiate a return request, book an appointment, update a customer record, or transfer the conversation to a human representative.

FastCom AI, a product of AI and software development company Ascend AI, is being developed for these customer-facing operations. Its approach combines AI conversations with the systems businesses already use behind the scenes.

The distinction is therefore about more than how naturally the software speaks. It also concerns the information it can access and the tasks it is authorised to perform.

FastCom connects customers with a company's existing systems, bringing together conversations from Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp, Instagram, web chat and email.

The AI can also integrate with customer relationship management (CRM) software, ticketing platforms, order and inventory systems, enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, and company knowledge bases.

This allows the agent to retrieve information from approved databases and business systems when responding to customers, rather than relying solely on prepared answers.

For an e-commerce business, that could mean checking product availability, confirming an order or providing a delivery update. For an electronics company, it could involve answering warranty questions, registering a service request or checking repair status.

An automobile company could use the system for model and price enquiries, test-drive bookings and after-sales service questions. Healthcare providers could use it for appointment bookings, doctor availability and report-status enquiries.

FastCom is also being designed around how customers communicate in Bangladesh. According to the company, the platform supports Bangla, Banglish and English, allowing customers to move between languages within a conversation.

A customer might ask about a product in Bangla, type its model name in English, send a follow-up in Banglish and then ask about delivery. Supporting these exchanges is particularly relevant where customer interactions rarely follow a fixed script.

Some of FastCom's earliest deployments in Bangladesh have been with F-commerce businesses, where much of the sales process takes place through Facebook and other messaging platforms.

FastCom says its system currently handles around 95% of customer conversations and associated order flows in some of these deployments. Cases requiring human judgement are passed to staff.

The company cited one seller as an example of how automation could change customer-service operations. Before deployment, the business had around 20 people involved in customer management.

Following the rollout, FastCom says two representatives handled exceptions and escalations while the AI managed most routine interactions. The account does not specify whether other staff were reassigned or left the business.

The company said customer-management costs fell by more than half and revenue increased by around 20% after deployment. Revenue changes, however, can reflect several factors beyond customer-service automation.

The potential benefits also extend beyond staffing costs. An AI system can respond outside normal working hours, so a customer who sends a late-night message can receive an answer without waiting until the following morning.

Routine enquiries can be handled separately from complaints and unusual cases requiring human attention. The system can also help businesses maintain a consistent response process regardless of when customers contact them.

FastCom is now being introduced to larger corporate businesses in Bangladesh, whose reasons for adopting the technology may differ from those of high-volume F-commerce sellers.

A business does not need to receive tens of thousands of messages a day to have a response-time problem.

FastCom says some businesses it previously worked with took an average of around two and a half hours to respond to an enquiry. In some deployments, that has fallen to roughly 25 seconds with AI handling the initial interaction.

"Companies are not looking at this only as a cost-saving tool," said Yaseen Nur, founder and CEO of Ascend AI. "For some of them, the bigger issue is that a customer should not have to wait two or three hours for an answer the company already has."

For these businesses, response speed can become part of the customer's experience of the brand. This is particularly relevant when an enquiry concerns information already available within the organisation.

Human intervention remains essential. One frustration with earlier chatbots was that customers could remain stuck in an automated conversation after the system had reached the limits of its ability to help.

FastCom includes human handover in its operating model. If the AI is not confident it can handle an interaction, the conversation can be escalated to a representative with its previous context attached.

This means the representative can continue the exchange without asking the customer to repeat everything.

Businesses can also determine the extent of the AI's authority. For sensitive uses, responses can be restricted to approved company information, and businesses can log actions for review and limit access to the systems and data required for a particular task.

These controls become more consequential as the technology gains the ability to act. An incorrect answer can cause problems, but an unauthorised change to a customer record, an incorrect service request or an unapproved promise can have wider operational consequences.

FastCom says its enterprise architecture includes confidence-based escalation, approved-answer controls and audit trails for AI actions. It also lists encryption, role-based access, and configurable data-retention controls among its security features.

Agentic AI remains in the early stages in Bangladesh, and deploying it requires more than activating a conversational interface.

The system needs accurate company information, clear policies, and appropriate integrations. Businesses must decide which actions they can perform automatically, which require approval, and when they must hand a conversation to a person.

FastCom describes a structured deployment process in which the platform connects to relevant business information and systems, then tests and adjusts against real customer traffic before a wider rollout.

The quality of that preparation will help determine whether AI agents can become a dependable part of customer service.

By participating in the work that follows an enquiry, these systems offer the prospect of faster responses, round-the-clock service, and lower operating costs. Their expanded role also raises the requirements for accuracy, security, and control.

For businesses, the test will be whether an AI agent can reliably determine when to answer, when to act, and when to transfer the conversation to a person.

Title: Woman's dismembered body found in briefcase, sack; 3 arrested
Content:
The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has arrested three people, including the victim's boyfriend, after identifying a woman whose dismembered body was recovered from a briefcase and a sack dumped in water beside the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway in Gazipur.

According to PBI, the murder was planned following a dispute over a marriage promise and financial matters.

The victim, identified as Dolly Akter, also known as Kalia, 30, was the younger sister of Sohel, 44, of Pahar Paboijan village in Muktagacha, Mymensingh.

She had been living alone in the Memberbari area of Baniarchala under Joydebpur Police Station following her divorce.

On 11 September, police recovered one part of a partially decomposed body from a briefcase found in water beside the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway and another part from a sack dumped nearby.

Dolly's elder brother Sohel later filed a case with Joydebpur Police Station against unidentified people on charges of murder and concealing the body.

PBI's Gazipur district unit took over the investigation on 12 September. A crime scene team led by Police Inspector Mohammad Mostafizur Rahman Ansari analysed records and intelligence information to identify the victim and determine the circumstances surrounding the killing.

As part of the investigation, PBI arrested Mishon Islam, his mother Banu Akter and his friend Mizanur Rahman Milton the same day.

According to PBI, a cleaver and blade allegedly used to dismember the body, Scotch tape used to package it, Dolly's national identity card, a button phone and her shoes were recovered from Mishon's room based on information he provided.

Investigators also collected CCTV footage showing the purchase of the suitcase allegedly used to transport the body.

PBI said Dolly met Mishon around five years ago while working at Tamanna Garments, and the two later became romantically involved.

A dispute subsequently developed between them over a marriage promise and financial matters, leading Mishon to allegedly plan Dolly's murder, according to the investigation.

PBI said Dolly went to Mishon's home on the night of 8 September and had an argument with his mother, Banu Akter. Dolly and Mishon later stayed in the same room.

According to PBI, Mishon gave Dolly sleeping medication as part of the alleged plan.

After she fell asleep, he allegedly strangled her with a lungi while pinning her down with his foot at around 2am. He then allegedly pressed a pillow over her face to ensure her death.

Mishon allegedly hid the body under a bed before buying a suitcase the following day. He then cut the body in half at the waist using a cleaver and blade, PBI said.

The lower part was placed in the suitcase, while the upper part was wrapped in polythene and put in a sack.

Later, Mishon and his mother allegedly called their acquaintance Mizanur Rahman Milton to their home, telling him they were moving house.

They then took the suitcase and sack to Bhabanipur and allegedly dumped them into a canal from Bhabanipur Bridge, according to PBI.

Investigators said blood got on Milton's hand while they were disposing of the body, after which Mishon told him what had happened. The three later returned to their respective homes.

PBI said all three accused gave confessional statements before a court on 13 September.

Abu Yusuf, superintendent of police at the PBI media wing, said the agency identified the victim and uncovered the circumstances of the murder by analysing data and intelligence after taking over the investigation.

He said three people allegedly involved in the killing had been arrested and key evidence recovered. PBI is investigating whether anyone else was involved, he added.

Title: Kallas calls says Israeli settlements should be treated like Russian-occupied Crimea
Content:
European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas has called for the bloc to ban trade with illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian Territories, arguing that the EU should apply the same approach it took to Russian-occupied Crimea.

Kallas said the EU should maintain a consistent approach to international law. When Russia annexed Crimea in 2014, the EU promptly banned trade with the peninsula, and she argued that the same principle should apply to occupied Palestinian territory, says the Middle East Eye.

The economic impact of a settlement trade ban would be limited because of the relatively small volume of goods involved, Kallas acknowledged, but she said the measure would carry major symbolic significance.

The proposal could also avoid the EU's requirement for unanimity on foreign policy decisions. Framing the measure as an EU trade policy would allow it to be approved by a qualified majority of member states.

EU-wide foreign policy sanctions against Israel have been blocked by opposition from countries including Germany, Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovenia.

Kallas said European institutions were facing increasing criticism over their failure to impose sanctions on Israel in response to its actions in Gaza. Several national governments have been pressing the European Commission to put forward an EU-wide trade ban.

UK sanctions and European pressure

The proposal follows a decision by the United Kingdom on 8 September to impose trade sanctions on Israeli settlements, including settlements in Syria's Golan Heights.

Ten other European countries and Canada signed a joint statement with Britain expressing their intention to introduce national restrictions or support EU-wide measures.

The moves followed Israel's approval in August of the E1 settlement project, which envisages construction of 3,400 new housing units in occupied Palestinian territory.

The settlement expansion has drawn international criticism and added to pressure on European governments to take further action.

Israeli and US backlash

Israel has responded to Britain's measures with diplomatic retaliation.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar closed the British consulate in East Jerusalem and barred 11 British Members of Parliament from entering Israel.

US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee also criticised British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, accusing him of "Jew hate" and threatening retaliation.

Kallas's position also marks a shift from some of her earlier public statements. She has reportedly compared Israel's treatment of Palestinians to apartheid South Africa in private, while in March 2025 she publicly expressed solidarity with Israel.

Title: Charge sheets filed against Hasina, 62 others in two Jatrabari cases
Content:
Police have submitted charge sheets against 63 people, including former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, in two separate cases filed over murder and attempted murder in the capital's Jatrabari area during the July Uprising.

Investigators have also recommended the discharge of 105 people after finding no evidence of their involvement in the offences.

Sub-Inspector Mohin Uddin of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's prosecution division confirmed the development, saying two sub-inspectors of Jatrabari Police Station separately submitted the charge sheets to the court. Hearings on whether to accept the charge sheets are scheduled to be held soon.

Nadim attempted murder case

In the attempted murder case filed with Jatrabari Police Station, Investigation Officer Sub-Inspector Ibrahim Khalil submitted a charge sheet against 30 people, including Sheikh Hasina, on 27 July. He also recommended the discharge of 66 people for lack of evidence.

Other accused include former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, former road transport and bridges minister Obaidul Quader, former food minister Advocate Kamrul Islam, former inspector general of police Chowdhury Abdullah Al-Mamun, former Dhaka Metropolitan Police commissioner Habibur Rahman, former Dhaka DB chief Harun Or Rashid, former DMP joint commissioner Biplob Kumar Sarker and former Chhatra League president Saddam Hossain.

A hearing on whether to accept the charge sheet is scheduled for 19 September.

According to the case statement, Tolaram College student Nadim joined the anti-discrimination movement at Rayerbagh bus stand in Jatrabari on 19 July 2024.

At the time, protesters came under attack and gunfire broke out. Nadim was shot in the left knee, with the bullet passing through.

He recovered after receiving treatment. Nadim filed the case against Sheikh Hasina and 93 others on 6 October 2024.

Babul Mridha murder case

In the murder case over the death of construction worker Md Babul Mridha during the July Movement, Jatrabari Police Station Sub-Inspector Mahmudul Hasan Irfan submitted a charge sheet against 33 people, including Sheikh Hasina, on 13 August.

The investigator also recommended the discharge of 39 people after finding no evidence of their involvement.

The accused include former road transport and bridges minister Obaidul Quader, former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, former law minister Anisul Huq, former foreign minister Hasan Mahmud, former state minister for information and broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat, former Dhaka South City Corporation mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh, former Jatrabari-5 lawmaker Kazi Monirul Islam Monu, former Patuakhali-3 lawmaker SM Shahzada, former Pirojpur-2 lawmaker Mohiuddin Maharaj, former Barishal-4 lawmaker Pankaj Nath and former Barishal City Corporation mayor Sadiq Abdullah.

Others include former IGP Chowdhury Abdullah Al-Mamun, former DMP commissioner Habibur Rahman, former Dhaka South unit Swechhasebak League president Kamrul Hasan Ripon, former Jatrabari thana Awami League general secretary Harunur Rashid Munna, former Bhandaria upazila parishad chairman Mirazul Islam Miraz and former Dhaka South unit Chhatra League general secretary Sajal Kundu.

A hearing on whether to accept the charge sheet is scheduled for Monday, said Sub-Inspector Mohiuddin Chowdhury of the DMP prosecution division.

According to the case statement, Babul Mridha left home on 19 July 2024 to look for his son Abu Taleb, who had joined the anti-discrimination student movement in the Dania and Lucky Community Centre areas of Jatrabari.

He was shot after reaching the Lucky Community Centre area. Locals rescued him and took him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where he received treatment for around a month.

He was later transferred to BGB Hospital and subsequently moved to Combined Military Hospital on 22 August. Babul Mridha died while undergoing treatment at CMH on 9 September 2024, 52 days after being shot. His wife, Seema Begum, filed the murder case with Jatrabari Police Station on 19 November 2024.

Title: Case filed against Khulshi OC, 8 others over alleged vandalism, looting in Ctg
Content:
A case has been filed in a Chattogram court against nine people, including Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Abdur Rahim of Khulshi Police Station, over allegations of illegally entering a house, vandalism, looting, assault and firing rubber bullets.

Md Jabed, 66, filed the case with the Chattogram Metropolitan Magistrate Court yesterday (13 September). He is the father of expelled Chattogram Metropolitan Jatiyatabadi Swechhasebak Dal joint convener Wakil Hossain alias Bihari Boga.

The plaintiff's lawyer, SM Moinul Islam, said the court took cognisance of the case and directed the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of police to investigate it.

Besides OC Mohammad Abdur Rahim, the accused are Sub-Inspector Shah Poran, Md Anwar Hossain, a member from the Jalalabad area, Jubo League member Babu alias Prakash, Md Mizanur Rahman from the Pahartali College area, Aman Ullah Aman from West Khulshi, and journalists Arif and Asad Ullah from Nasirabad Housing Society.

According to the case petition, the accused illegally entered Jabed's house at Wireless intersection in Ward 13 of Pahartali under Khulshi Police Station at around 4:30am on 4 September.

Jabed alleged that the accused vandalised the house, looted valuables, assaulted residents and fired rubber bullets during the incident.

He alleged that after entering the residential quarters, the accused vandalised furniture, doors, windows and other belongings, causing damage worth around Tk3 lakh.

They later entered the room of his daughter-in-law, Rekha Begum, broke open a wardrobe and took Tk8 lakh in cash and around three bhori of gold ornaments, according to the case petition. The plaintiff claimed total losses of around Tk17 lakh.

Earlier, on 29 August, a case was filed with Khulshi Police Station over allegations of abducting and assaulting a teacher of Pahartali College. Jabed's son Wakil Hossain was named as an accused in that case.

Police claimed that they conducted a raid early on 4 September to arrest Wakil in connection with the case, when his followers put up barricades on the road, attacked police and vandalised police vehicles.

Following the incident, police filed a separate case naming 21 people and 250 unidentified others.

Title: Customs seizes foreign cigarettes, vapes, mobile phone displays at Dhaka airport
Content:
Customs intelligence officials have seized foreign cigarettes, vapes and mobile phone displays from passengers at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.

The seized goods-223 cartons of foreign cigarettes, 44 vapes and 144 -have an estimated value of Tk 17.46 lakh, according to the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate.

Acting on a tip-off received on 13 September, officials of the Airport Customs Intelligence and Investigation Circle, B-shift, stepped up surveillance of passengers arriving on various international flights.

A passenger identified as Abdul Karim, who arrived from Dubai on Emirates flight EK584, was stopped for a baggage check while crossing the Green Channel after his luggage appeared suspicious.

A subsequent search and inventory found 223 cartons of foreign cigarettes in his baggage, which were seized by customs officials.

On the same day, customs officials searched the baggage of Shepon, a passenger arriving from Malaysia on AirAsia flight AK71, and recovered 44 vapes.

In another operation, officials recovered 98 mobile phone displays from KM Tofail Ahmed, a passenger arriving from Guangzhou on US-Bangla Airlines flight BS326.

They also recovered another 46 mobile phone displays from Shamima Akter, who arrived on the same flight.

The two passengers were carrying a total of 144 mobile phone displays.

Customs intelligence officials are examining whether the incidents are linked to organised smuggling networks and whether passengers were being used as carriers for smuggled goods.

Title: Outsider detained over alleged harassment of SUST student
Content:
Security personnel at Shahjalal University of Science and Technology (SUST) detained an outsider yesterday night (13 September) for allegedly harassing a female student on campus.

The security staff detained 27-year-old Anarul Mia in front of the university's teachers' quarters and took him to the Proctor's Office. He was later handed over to police.

Victim said Anarul followed her on a motorcycle while she was returning to her dormitory after a tutoring session. At one point, he stopped his motorcycle, asked for her mobile phone number and proposed becoming friends. He also allegedly made several indecent remarks.

The student then informed her friends about the incident over the phone. University security personnel subsequently arrived at the scene, detained Anarul and took him to the Proctor's Office.

Shoaibur Rahman, a university security guard, said, "We detained him in front of the teachers' quarters. Many students gathered there later. He was then taken to the Proctor's Office."

University Proctor Professor Md. Mokhlesur Rahman said the accused was handed over to the police.

"Proper action will be taken against him in accordance with the law and the university will provide all necessary support to the victim," he said.

Title: Infinix reports top spot in Bangladesh smartphone market, citing IDC data
Content:
Infinix said it remained Bangladesh's No. 1 smartphone brand throughout 2025 and retained that position in the first and second quarters of 2026, citing market data from International Data Corporation (IDC).

The company attributed its continued position to an expanding product portfolio that caters to different consumer needs and budgets, according to a press release.

Over the past few years, Infinix has introduced smartphones in Bangladesh ranging from affordable everyday devices to models focused on performance and gaming. Its recent line-up includes the NOTE 60 Series, GT 30 Series, HOT 70 Series and SMART 20 Series.

The company said these product lines offered options for students, young professionals, users seeking entertainment features and mobile gamers.

The NOTE 60 Series is positioned as an all-round option for users seeking a combination of performance, display quality, camera capabilities and battery life.

The recently introduced NOTE 60 and NOTE 60 Pro target consumers who use their smartphones for work, entertainment, photography and multitasking. Infinix said the series was designed to meet the everyday needs of young professionals and students.

For gaming enthusiasts, the GT 30 Series focuses on performance, with gaming features, high-refresh-rate displays and technologies designed to support sustained gameplay.

The company said the series targeted users who spend considerable time gaming on their smartphones. The GT 30 Pro, in particular, targets consumers who prioritise gaming performance and responsiveness.

The HOT 70 Series serves the mainstream market, combining design, everyday performance, entertainment features and battery capabilities.

The HOT 70 and HOT 70 Pro 5G offer different options within the series. The Pro 5G adds 5G connectivity and enhanced performance for consumers seeking more advanced features, the company said.

At the more affordable end of the portfolio, the SMART 20 Series caters to students, first-time smartphone users and consumers seeking practical devices for communication, online learning, social media and entertainment.

Infinix said the series focused on essential smartphone functions to provide an accessible option for everyday use.

Together, the product lines address a range of lifestyles, budgets and usage patterns in Bangladesh. The company said it developed devices for different consumer groups and broadened its presence across market segments.

Infinix attributed its reported market position in 2025 and the first and second quarters of 2026 to the relevance of this product strategy in Bangladesh's competitive smartphone market.

The company said the achievement reflected consumer confidence in its combination of technology, affordability and design, and strengthened its brand credibility in Bangladesh.

Title: Oil markets survived the Iran war sprint. Now comes the marathon
Content:
The widening of the Mideast conflict into Yemen and drone strikes on a critical Saudi oil pipeline highlight an uncomfortable reality: the Iran war is no longer a short-lived energy supply shock, but a prolonged, unpredictable test of global economic endurance.

With crude oil back above $100 a barrel, markets are adjusting to a new and more volatile phase of the conflict, one in which many of the safeguards that cushioned the initial blow nearly seven months ago have disappeared.

US President Donald Trump predicted last week that the conflict would end only after the US midterm elections on 3 November. This is a notable shift in tone from an administration that initially suggested the war would last weeks, not months.

Whether this new forecast proves correct is impossible to know, but recent developments at two of the world's most important energy arteries suggest it may be very optimistic.

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have made rapid advances over the past week, tightening their grip on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern entrance to the Red Sea. The group announced a naval blockade of the shipping route in July and has reiterated that transit remains safe for all vessels except those belonging to Saudi Arabia.

At the same time, Saudi Arabia's vital East-West oil pipeline, the kingdom's main alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, was temporarily shut after a series of drone attacks launched from Iraq, according to Saudi authorities.

The 1,200-kilometre (745-mile) pipeline has been critical for the kingdom since the Strait of Hormuz began to be disrupted following the outbreak of the war in February.

By more than doubling west coast exports via the pipeline during the first five months of the conflict to 4 million to 5 million barrels per day (bpd), equal to roughly 4% to 5% of global oil supply, Saudi Arabia was able to offset a significant portion of the losses through Hormuz.

Yet those shipments fell to just 2 million bpd in August, the lowest since January, largely because of the Houthi blockade, according to Kpler data. In turn, output from what was once the world's largest oil exporter fell to 6 million bpd in August, the lowest level in more than three decades, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA).

Satellite imagery suggests that at least one pumping station was struck, although the full extent of the damage and the timeline for repairs remain unclear. Saudi Arabia will also likely be able to draw on stored crude to offset any interruption in pipeline flows for several days. But this escalation comes at a dangerous moment.

Disruption to Middle East oil exports, which accounted for around a fifth of global supplies before the war, has sharply eroded global stocks. Inventories have fallen by 507 million barrels, or roughly 2.8 million bpd, since the conflict began, according to the IEA.

It's true that more crude has been exiting Hormuz in recent months compared to the early months of the war, largely because more vessels have been using a route along Oman's coast under US Navy supervision. Around 5 million bpd of crude oil and refined products have been exported through the strait since June, around a quarter of pre-war levels, according to Kpler, though the real figure may be higher because many ships switch off their navigation systems during transit.

Iranian strikes on over a dozen tankers attempting to cross Hormuz or inside the Gulf last week were a reminder that transits remain risky.

Regardless, this status quo is unsustainable. The Middle East remains the most important energy-producing region in the world. Halving crude exports from the Gulf may be manageable for a few months, but certainly not indefinitely.

Moreover, refined products like diesel, gasoline and jet fuel have fared considerably worse than crude, with exports from the region remaining nearly 60% below pre-war levels, according to IEA estimates. This has led to acute fuel shortages, particularly of diesel, pushing prices to record levels. Further disruption to Saudi Arabia's Red Sea exports would put additional pressure on global inventories.

This latest flare-up could also cause ship traffic through Hormuz to shrink once again. Tanker operators remain reluctant to enter conflict zones, freight and insurance costs have surged to all-time highs and naval escorts can only partially mitigate the risks of operating in a war zone.

The question now is just how long these market dynamics can hold.

Iran's leadership views the conflict as existential and has every reason to maximise economic pressure on both the US and the wider global economy ahead of any eventual negotiations.

At the same time, Washington's increasingly stringent blockade of Iranian oil exports is inflicting severe damage on the Islamic Republic's economy, raising the costs of extending the confrontation indefinitely.

The Houthi advances and attacks on Saudi infrastructure may temporarily shift momentum back towards Tehran.

Those competing pressures could eventually bring both sides closer to the negotiating table. Equally, they could encourage each camp to keep fighting in the hope that economic or military gains will strengthen its bargaining position.

For nearly seven months, markets assumed Trump would find an off-ramp once rising gasoline prices and political costs became too painful. But that outcome depended on Tehran being willing to cooperate. So far, it has shown little interest in doing so.

US policymakers and traders may have become accustomed to a conflict that appears manageable.

But if the war drags on for many more months, as Trump now suggests it might, the risk is that new disruption would find the market with far fewer shock absorbers.

Ron Bousso is the Reuters Energy Columnist

Title: ICT verdict in July crimes case against Quader, 6 others tomorrow
Content:
The International Crimes Tribunal will deliver its verdict tomorrow (15 September) in the case against seven top leaders of the banned Awami League, including its General Secretary Obaidul Quader, over alleged crimes against humanity committed during the July Uprising.

A three-member International Crimes Tribunal-2, headed by Justice Md Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, set the date today (14 September).

Earlier, on 17 August, the tribunal kept the case awaiting verdict after the completion of closing arguments. The recording of evidence concluded on 2 August, with 29 prosecution witnesses, including the investigation officer, testifying in the case.

The other accused are Awami League Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, former state minister for information and broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat, Jubo League President Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, General Secretary Moinul Hossain Khan Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hussain and General Secretary Wali Asif Enan.

All seven accused are currently absconding.

On 22 January this year, Tribunal-2 framed charges against the seven accused and ordered the trial to begin. Earlier, on 18 December last year, the same tribunal took cognisance of the formal charges submitted by the prosecution.

According to the prosecution, the accused jointly issued directives and made provocative and inciting statements to suppress the July-August movement. They also held several meetings to plan violence and called on party leaders and activists to take to the streets and build resistance against the protesters.

The prosecution further alleged that the accused played roles in armed attacks, severe repression, and controlling the media in some areas.

Their actions resulted in killings, attempted killings and widespread violence across the country, which constitute crimes against humanity punishable under the law, according to the prosecution.

Title: Infant dies at Padma General Hospital; health directorate chief inspects facility amid negligence allegations
Content:
A nine-month-old infant died yesterday (13 September) while undergoing treatment at Padma General Hospital in the capital, with his relatives alleging medical negligence and the absence of a doctor.

The hospital authorities, however, said the child, Ayan Abdullah, died after suddenly suffering a cardiac arrest.

Following the incident, Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) Director General (Additional) Zahid Raihan arrived at Padma General Hospital this morning (14 September) and inspected the facility.

He is expected to brief journalists regarding the matter later.

Following Ayan's death around 9pm yesterday, his Asif Hasan made the allegations during a Facebook Live around midnight.

The video later spread across social media.

According to Asif, Ayan had been undergoing treatment at the hospital for the past 13 days for diabetes-related complications.

He said Ayan was normal until the afternoon of the day he died.

In the evening, while family members were trying to feed him, his body gradually began turning blue.

Asif said family members were later suddenly informed that the child needed life support.

When they asked to see him, the hospital authorities allegedly did not allow them to do so. As his condition deteriorated, doctors later declared him dead, he said.

Medical Officer of the hospital Dr Najmul Huq said the child suddenly suffered a cardiac arrest and stopped breathing at one stage.

"We had plans to discharge the child from the hospital the very next day," he said.

Hospital authorities said they would investigate whether there had been any medical negligence and take necessary action if evidence of negligence was found. They asked for some time to conduct the investigation.

Tension at hospital following death

Following news of the child's death, tension and a commotion broke out between the relatives and hospital staff. Police went to the hospital after receiving the news last night.

Hospital authorities alleged that agitated relatives destroyed medicines and medical supplies and assaulted several nurses.

However, they could not produce any CCTV footage to support the allegations.

The child's relatives denied the allegations, claiming that hospital staff had attacked them first.

Burial without autopsy

Complications also arose over whether the child's body would undergo an autopsy.

The relatives said the child's mother would not be able to bear seeing Ayan's body cut open for an autopsy. They therefore took the body away for burial soon after his death.

The relatives, however, said they would take necessary legal action if evidence of medical negligence was found later.

Administrative Officer of Padma General Hospital, Jahirul Islam Anik, rejected the allegations of negligence in duty.

He said action would be taken if the allegations were substantiated through an investigation.

Title: Tucker Carlson says Israel seeks regional hegemony through Iran war
Content:
Right-wing political commentator Tucker Carlson has claimed that Israel pushed for war with Iran as part of a strategy to establish regional hegemony, arguing that the conflict also serves to weaken Gulf Arab states and reduce US military influence in the Persian Gulf.

In an interview with Going Underground , Carlson said Israel's objectives included expanding its borders and eliminating threats posed by Iran and its regional allies, including Hezbollah and Hamas, says the Middle East Eye.

Carlson also argued that Israel views the economic growth and development of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states - Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates - as a "massive threat" to its regional dominance.

He rejected the view that US military bases in the Gulf primarily benefit Israel, instead describing them as "control mechanisms" or "leashes" that constrain Israel's freedom of action.

Carlson said a central objective of the conflict was therefore to force a US military withdrawal from the Gulf.

Carlson said he had warned US President Donald Trump about his assessment during a meeting in the Oval Office around February 20. He said he told Trump that the push for war was driven by a desire for Israeli regional hegemony and warned him that "this is actually aimed at us".

Carlson also questioned why Trump had allowed events to unfold in a way that severely damaged Gulf states, given the president's warm personal relationships with their leaders.

The conflict has had wider consequences across the Gulf. According to the information cited by Carlson, Iran fired thousands of missiles and drones at targets across all six GCC states, spreading the financial and logistical costs of the war across the region.

Saudi Arabia also closed its East-West oil pipeline after drone attacks attributed to militants based in Iraq, while key energy infrastructure across the region sustained damage.

Satellite imagery analysis cited in the source found that at least 228 buildings or pieces of equipment at US military sites in the region had been damaged or destroyed.

Persistent attacks on US military facilities have also prompted the Pentagon to evaluate whether Washington should reduce its military presence in the Persian Gulf.

Gulf states, meanwhile, have been recalibrating foreign investments as the financial costs of the conflict reduce revenues, seeking to preserve their economic influence globally while managing increased wartime spending.
